papers.title: Preoperative Factors Associated With Pulmonary Embolism Following Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty: An ACS-NSQIP Analysis of 2017–2021 Data
papers.abstract: Background This study examined preoperative factors associated with 30-day pulmonary embolism (PE) after primary total hip arthroplasty. Methods ACS-NSQIP records from 2017–2021 with CPT code 27130 were analyzed. Complete cases were included using cleaned body mass index (BMI), age, sex, steroid use, and disseminated cancer. These five variables were entered jointly into logistic regression. Results Among 196,495 complete cases, 484 (0.246%) had PE. Adjusted odds ratios were 6.44 for disseminated cancer, 1.69 for steroid use, 1.23 for female sex, 1.041 per year of age, and 1.031 per kg/m² of BMI (all P < .05). Apparent AUC was 0.647 (95% CI, 0.622–0.672). The Hosmer–Lemeshow test indicated lack of fit (P = .012). Conclusions Five preoperative characteristics were associated with PE. Discrimination was modest, calibration limitations were present, and validation is required before clinical use.

papers.title: STEAM and Computational Thinking in Technology-Enhanced Education: A Systematic Review of Learning Design
papers.abstract: This systematic literature review examines how STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics) and computational thinking (CT) activities are conceptualized and implemented in technology-enhanced learning environments in primary and lower secondary education. Guided by PRISMA 2020 procedures, 34 empirical studies were analyzed using inductive content analysis to identify recurring pedagogical structures. Seven categories emerged: problem-based, inquiry-based, and project-based pedagogical forms; a social dimension of collaborative learning; and modal formats including role-playing, game-based, and experiential learning. These categories reflect patterns of pedagogical organization rather than disciplinary content alone. Interpreted through the lens of active learning, the findings indicate that STEAM and CT activities are predominantly structured as activity-centered, interdisciplinary, and iterative learning processes. CT appears not as an isolated technological skill but as a structuring principle for organizing reasoning, problem decomposition, and solution refinement across subject domains. Overall, the reviewed studies suggest that STEAM–CT integration increasingly functions as a model of learning design and orchestration: CT organizes sequences of cognitive actions, while active learning formats cultivate epistemic practices (investigating, designing, testing, and refining) realized through the interaction of tools, artifacts, and collaborative structures. This positioning highlights STEAM and CT as integral to contemporary science, mathematics, and technology education.

papers.title: Coupling Multi-Temporal Satellite InSAR Ground Subsidence and Extreme Value Theory Rainfall Modeling for Urban Flood Vulnerability in Greater Accra, Ghana
papers.abstract: Urban flash flood vulnerability assessments conventionally treat digital elevation models (DEMs) as temporally static surfaces. However, rapidly urbanizing coastal metropolises across the Global South frequently experience substantial, ongoing land subsidence that alters surface hydraulic gradients over decadal baselines. This study presents an integrated computational framework coupling multi-temporal Synthetic Aperture Radar interferometry (InSAR), statistical Extreme Value Theory (EVT), and physics-informed machine learning to quantify flood inundation across Greater Accra, Ghana. Daily precipitation records (1990 to 2024; 12,784 observations calibrated via CHIRPS/ERA5) were analyzed using Peaks-Over-Threshold (POT) sampling with a Generalized Pareto Distribution (GPD) fitted via Maximum Likelihood Estimation, establishing 5, 10, 25, 50, and 100-year design rainstorms. Multi-temporal Sentinel-1 C-band radar displacement fields (calibrated with multi-frequency NISAR interfaces) were decomposed into vertical subsidence rates, revealing three distinct kinematic subsidence bowls with peak downward velocities reaching -35.0 mm/year centered over the Odaw River Basin, Kwame Nkrumah Circle, Weija, and Glefe. A Dynamic Hydraulic Inundation Index (DHII) was formulated and modeled using an ensemble HistGradientBoosting classifier alongside a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) enforcing 2D Saint-Venant shallow water continuity. The machine learning architecture achieved strong rare-event discrimination (AUC-PR = 0.9596, Matthews Correlation Coefficient = 0.8341, accuracy = 90.75%), while the PINN converged to a shallow water PDE residual of 0.000204, predicting a 1.69 m inundation depth at Kwame Nkrumah Circle during a 50-year storm, aligning with municipal survey marks. Results demonstrate that differential ground subsidence systematically flattens natural drainage gradients, transforming ordinary corridors into hydraulic flood traps. Open-Source Code Repository: https://github.com/eminent337/accra-insar-extreme-rainfall Keywords: InSAR, Extreme Value Theory, Generalized Pareto Distribution, Ground Subsidence, Flash Flooding, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, Accra Ghana, Open-Source Geosciences.

papers.title: Vitamin C-Induced Photo-Redox Threshold Enables High-Fidelity Volumetric Printing of Collagen.
papers.abstract: Tomographic volumetric printing (TVP) enables rapid fabrication of complex, centimeter-scale 3D architectures. TVP of native proteins such as collagen is attractive because it preserves native bioactive motifs that regulate cell-matrix signaling. However, direct TVP of collagen remains challenging because dityrosine crosslinking, driven by visible-light-activated Ru(II)bpy3 2+/sodium persulfate (SPS), lacks an effective inhibitory mechanism. This results in near-immediate crosslinking upon light exposure, leading to an insufficient nonlinear threshold response that fails to suppress background curing. Here, we introduce vitamin C (L-ascorbic acid) as a biocompatible redox regulator to overcome this limitation. We demonstrated that vitamin C established a photo-redox threshold by suppressing Ru(III) accumulation and scavenging persulfate radicals within the Ru/SPS system, thereby delaying dityrosine crosslinking until vitamin C depletion. This threshold generated the nonlinear response required for TVP, enabling high-fidelity volumetric printing of collagen. Post-printing construct densification (∼53% shrinkage) further improved feature resolution (80 µm positive; 120 µm negative) and yielded mechanically stable and highly stretchable hydrogels (up to 180% strain). Collagen resin with vitamin C supported both cell seeding post-printing and cell-laden printing with high cell density and viability, enabling the rapid biofabrication of cell-instructive 3D microenvironments.

papers.title: Curcumin-loaded alkali-heat-treated titanium modulates macrophage inflammatory responses.
papers.abstract: Chronic inflammation at the implant-tissue interface is a major contributor to implant failure. Therefore, enhancing the biological response of titanium (Ti) surfaces is critical for promoting early osseointegration and improving long-term implant stability. In this study, alkali-heat-treated (AHT) Ti was evaluated as a platform for the controlled delivery of curcumin (Cur), a natural anti-inflammatory compound. The release kinetics of curcumin and the interactions between curcumin-loaded AHT Ti surfaces and RAW264.7 macrophages were investigated in vitro. Various polymer coating strategies were applied to modulate curcumin release. The presence of poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) reduced the curcumin release under both physiological (pH 7.4) and acidic (pH 5.0) conditions, with uncoated AHT samples exhibiting the greatest cumulative release (∼21.3 μg) in Study 1. Increasing the loaded curcumin amount from 100 to 300 μg resulted in a decrease in the release for both pH 7.4 and pH 5.0, whereas the incorporation of polyethylene glycol/polycaprolactone (PEG/PCL) coating enhanced the gradual curcumin release (Study 2). Increasing the curcumin loading from 50 to 100 and 300 μg increased the total amount of curcumin released, with the 300 μg group exhibiting a more gradual release profile. However, the percentage of curcumin released decreased as the loading amount increased (Study 3). When macrophages were cultured on Ti surfaces, AHT samples exhibited higher cell viability than polished (P) control samples, and the presence of curcumin reduced cell viability in a dose-dependent manner. While macrophages cultured on AHT surfaces exhibited a transient increase in pro-inflammatory marker expression at 24 h compared with polished surfaces, the expression of these markers was reduced by 48 h. Notably, curcumin significantly decreased pro-inflammatory cytokine expression at both the gene and protein levels and suppressed NF-κB activation in macrophages exposed to inflammatory stimuli. Overall, the sustained and controlled release of curcumin from AHT Ti surface is highly dependent on the curcumin loading amount as well as the presence and composition of the polymer coating. Moreover, both AHT and curcumin significantly reduced inflammatory responses in macrophages, demonstrating the potential of the curcumin-loaded AHT Ti platform as an immunomodulatory surface for improving the biological performance and long-term success of Ti implants.

papers.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning enables mobile robots to make fast and scalable navigation decisions in constrained human-shared environments. However, directly extending single-robot approaches to multi-robot settings often fails to ensure safety and efficiency, especially under occlusions and out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios, where individual robots may overlook potential risks or make inaccurate predictions. Leveraging cooperation effectively for both prediction and navigation remains a major challenge. We propose CoopUQ, a multi-robot social navigation framework that bridges uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasting and robust decision making. CoopUQ predicts future occupancy grid maps through cross-robot spatiotemporal feature fusion and further leverages forecasts and their uncertainty to guide policy via constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning, where the cost penalizes navigation through regions predicted to be occupied or highly uncertain. This design enables the policy to adapt its risk sensitivity under distribution shifts. Experimental results across multiple Unity3D-based simulation environments with both in-distribution and OOD settings, including diverse layouts, pedestrian densities, and rushing behavior, demonstrate improved prediction performance and safety over representative baselines. Real-robot experiments further demonstrate its robustness across various scenes. Our code and videos are available at https://coopuq.github.io/.

papers.title: AnyGoal: On World Model Generalization Beyond Expert Rollouts
papers.abstract: The goal of a world model is to capture the dynamics of an environment. This has the great appeal that it allows agents to plan and simulate a course of actions with the help of a world model. For these uses to be reliable, however, the learned dynamics must behave well beyond the specific state-action combinations observed in expert rollouts. Despite this, the relationship between data coverage, dynamics generalization, and downstream planning performance remains underexplored. We study this relationship through the lens of compositional generalization: can a world model recombine familiar state and action factors into valid dynamics? To answer this, we introduce AnyGoal, a benchmark of goal-shifted task variants built from widely used world-model environments, together with an open-source library. Each task is designed to be within reach of a world model that has learned the underlying dynamics: individual state factors and actions remain within their training support, but their combinations are underrepresented in expert trajectories. Across multiple environments and world model families, we find that current models consistently exhibit failures under these recombinations. By examining dynamics and representation failures across model families, interaction regimes, and evaluation metrics, we study where current world models generalize and where challenges remain for goal-shifted prediction and planning. Together, this framework, benchmark, and analysis provide a basis for evaluating progress toward world models that generalize to new planning tasks.

papers.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
papers.abstract: Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world. However, scaling such learning directly in real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce substantial security risks. We therefore propose Agent World Model in the Wild (WildAWM), a scalable pipeline for synthesizing controllable environments and tasks for training general computer-use agents (CUAs). Whereas existing approaches typically specialize in a single agent interaction interface, we construct executable environments that jointly support graphical user interfaces, model context protocol services, and command-line interfaces, allowing agents to flexibly combine visual interaction, tool use, and code execution. WildAWM is entirely powered by open-source models, demonstrating that high-quality computer-use environments can be generated without proprietary frontier models. Beyond environments, we address three recurring challenges in task synthesis: ensuring solvability, maintaining sufficient difficulty, and producing reliable verifiers, by introducing execution-based quality gates that combine heterogeneous agent rollouts, cross-judge consistency checks, and counterfactual probes of judgment robustness. The resulting pipeline synthesizes 341 long-horizon environment-task pairs that can require over 100 agent steps to solve and remain challenging even for frontier models, with GPT-6-Astra solving only 60% of them. We train two Qwen models of different sizes exclusively in these synthetic worlds. Both models achieve substantial gains across 8 out-of-distribution benchmarks spanning web, claw, and computer-use agents, demonstrating that learning in WildAWM's synthesized worlds generalizes broadly to unseen computer-use tasks. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/MSR-Orchard/WildAWM.

papers.title: Next Best Action: Causal Constrained Offline RL for Business Action Targeting
papers.abstract: Next Best Action (NBA) systems must select among customer interventions (e.g., discounts, promotions, and lifecycle actions), maximize long-term economic value, satisfy complex operational constraints, and remain causally grounded. Existing approaches lack a rigorous framework for meeting these requirements jointly. We address this gap by formulating NBA as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP). We then integrate off-policy causal correction of the estimated customer dynamics directly into the Linear Programming (LP) formulation of the CMDP. The resulting policy selects actions based on customer states to maximize long-term value while explicitly enforcing business guardrails. Furthermore, the LP formulation yields shadow prices that quantify the economic trade-offs of operational constraints (e.g., fairness and user welfare), enhancing policy interpretability. The proposed controller formulates the thruster-assisted spring-loaded inverted pendulum dynamics as a condensed QP-based model predictive control problem, enabling simultaneous regulation of ground contact force and active thrust vectoring at 500 Hz. A decoupled control architecture is used, where the robot's sagittal dynamics are controlled using QP-MPC while the frontal dynamics is regulated using a cascade orientation stabilization controller. Two experiments were conducted with different forward reference velocities of 0 m/s and 0.1 m/s. While the instantaneous velocity oscillates, the mean velocities can track their respective reference. Additionally, joint tracking error remains within 1 deg while tracking the desired leg length given by the leg trajectory controller and desired swing trajectory given by Raibert's heuristic. The QP-MPC problem is consistently solved with 0.18ms, which is well within the 2ms computation budget while satisfying the GRF friction cone constraint.

papers.title: Physics-Constrained Modeling and Inference of the Equation of State for Dissociative Materials
papers.abstract: Equations of state (EOSs) describe how a material's internal energy and pressure change with temperature and density. They are inputs to hydrodynamic simulations in materials science and planetary science. We model the ion-thermal free-energy term for dissociative materials, where molecular bonds break apart to form new species under extreme conditions. This term is governed by two latent physical processes, a molar-mass surface and a Debye-temperature curve, neither of which is observed directly. Instead, both must be recovered from internal energy and pressure, which are derivatives of the free energy, subject to thermodynamic constraints. Existing EOS tables are typically built through material-specific hand-tuning, a process that is tedious, does not scale across materials or conditions, and offers no guarantee of thermodynamic consistency. We propose a partitioned statistical framework that infers molar mass and Debye temperature directly from EOS data, guaranteeing thermodynamic consistency by construction. Local molar-mass behavior is captured with polynomial basis functions across domain partitions, while the Debye temperature is modeled with an I-spline basis. In simulations and a carbon dioxide case study, the method accurately recovers the underlying physical quantities, improves prediction of held-out energy and pressure data, and provides uncertainty quantification while scaling with EOS table size.

papers.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Market Making on Prediction-Market Order Books
papers.abstract: A market maker provides liquidity by quoting prices to buy and sell an asset, earning the spread while managing inventory risk. We study market makers trained with multi-agent reinforcement learning on prediction markets, specifically Polymarket, whose thin order books pose distinct challenges. Three challenges underpin this research: adverse selection may cause a policy trained on real data to stop quoting; the consequences of a quote can arrive many steps after the action; and prediction-market L2 data does not identify individual orders needed for simulation. We address these challenges by reconstructing order-level LOBSTER-format data from Polymarket and training agents in JaxMARL-HFT on 417 real markets. We enrich the baseline market maker's observation space with the book and recent flow, redesign its actions and inventory controls, and propose a cooperative multi-agent decomposition into a quoter and a risk manager trained using recurrent Independent Proximal Policy Optimisation (IPPO) with RNN policies. We investigate reward shaping, particularly reward blending and post-fill markout, to mitigate credit-assignment difficulties between the agents. Our redesigned single-agent market maker quotes more frequently and incurs smaller held-out losses than the retrained JaxMARL-HFT baseline, although the contributions of jointly changed observations, actions and risk constraints are not separately identified. Decomposition alone performs poorly; careful reward design substantially improves the desk relative to the unshaped split and yields our best result. Models are evaluated on realised end-of-episode portfolio value on held-out markets. None establishes positive average portfolio value in periodic held-out evaluation, and each configuration was trained with one seed. The environment, data and protocol lay a foundation for makers that quote many linked markets at once.

Simulation evaluates full tactile, binary touch, and proprioception-only observations on 12 unseen objects; hardware experiments evaluate full tactile policies on ten objects under multiple hand orientations. In simulation, full tactile observations increase mean normalized rotation per episode over proprioception alone by 94.8% for the anthropomorphic hand and 66.9% for the symmetric hand, with longer mean episode durations and lower mean total fingertip loads. Overall, the symmetric hand achieves a 32.0% higher mean rotation count and a 25.8% higher aggregate rotation rate, together with longer manipulation duration. Additional hardware force recordings show a 19.9% lower mean total fingertip load for this layout. These findings relate finger arrangement to contact organization and load sharing, and show that richer tactile information supports greater task progress at lower mean loading in both simulated embodiments.

papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning enables learning high-performance control policies, but its reliance on extensive interaction limits deployment on physical systems where data collection is costly, and failures are unsafe. PIA pretrains a world model on heterogeneous low- and high-fidelity simulated trajectories, then adapts it with limited target-domain interaction using uncertainty-regularized planning. Rather than requiring an accurate simulator for policy transfer, PIA treats simulated trajectories as biased priors whose residual mismatch is corrected during online adaptation. We evaluate PIA in autonomous racing using high-fidelity simulation and on a real full-size autonomous race car. In simulation, PIA adapts faster across track and surface shifts than strong baselines, achieving lower lap times and fewer failures. On hardware, PIA achieves reliable few-shot adaptation with less than one hour of on-vehicle interaction.

papers.title: Holi-World: Building Holistic World Intelligence from Human-Ego Experience
papers.abstract: Human egocentric experience offers a rich foundation for learning how the world is organized and how it changes through interaction. Realizing this potential at scale requires turning growing volumes of recordings into learning resources that connect scene structure, object semantics, and interaction histories across viewpoints and time, while reducing dependence on costly manual annotation. We introduce HOLI-WORLD, an integrated ecosystem connecting experience capture, world representation, automated data construction, model learning, and independent evaluation. To sup- port learning at scale, HOLIWORLD-Foundry combines complementary static and dynamic perception to automatically construct world records that connect persistent scene structure and evolving object states with interaction histories and supporting observations. HOLIWORLD-Data organizes these records from approximately 100 self-collected scenes into grounded learning resources, including approximately 80K QA pairs used to train HOLIWORLD-VL-4B. Independent human annotations of heldout recordings form HOLIWORLD-Bench, supporting evaluation of both annotation quality and learned spatial and temporal understanding. Experiments on ScanNet, ScanNet++, Aria Digital Twin, and HOLIWORLD-Bench demonstrate strong performance in static perception and dynamic tracking, while training on HOLIWORLD-Data substantially improves HOLIWORLD-VL-4B's spatial and temporal reasoning on HOLI- WORLD-Bench and EgoDynamic4D. HOLIWORLD provides a practical foundation for expanding learning resources from the continuous flow of human experience and advancing machine understanding of the dynamic world.

papers.title: R2-GP: Variance-Calibrated Priors for Additive Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: We develop R2-GP, an R2D2-type prior for Gaussian process (GP) generalised additive models (GAMs) that calibrates explained variance ($R^2$) for Matérn covariance kernels. The function variance for standard Matérn kernels depends jointly on the effect magnitude and length-scale. As such, smooth and rough components with identical amplitudes contribute very different amounts of variation. With independent priors on component amplitudes, this variation results in variance overestimation, especially in higher dimensions. We overcome this by taking direct control over each component's expected contribution to prior explained variance. We do this by rescaling each component based on its length scale and observed inputs, and modelling each rescaled variance as a share of the function variance induced by a global $R^2$ prior. This allows R2-GP to scale well to many components. To also scale to large sample sizes, we extend R2-GP to Hilbert space approximation methods, a framework for kernels exploiting their spectral decompositions for fast and efficient inference. Our simulations and real-world case studies demonstrate superior generalisation and parameter recovery over independent variance priors.

papers.title: ForagerSim: Evaluating Embodied Map-Based Reasoning in Large-Scale Dynamic Worlds
papers.abstract: Animals build cognitive maps of vast environments, use them to perform map-based navigation, and might even be reusing the same circuitry used in spatial reasoning for creating and using maps of arbitrary task-spaces. In contrast, current embodied AI systems either rely on hand-engineered mapping pipelines, which break in the presence of unmodeled dynamics and are restricted to metric space, or on learned policies that rarely form map-like representations at all. Developing architectures that could learn to build and use map-like representations as flexibly as animals is, however, difficult because few embodied AI benchmarks actually require map-based reasoning. To address this, we present ForagerSim --- an interdisciplinary research platform and simulation environment focused on embodied tasks that require map-based reasoning, with scenarios ranging from mobile-robot search and rescue to animal foraging in both complex mazes and vast, potentially infinite open areas. ForagerSim is highly modular and allows modifying independent axes of difficulty related to perception (abstract 2D sensing to full RGB or LiDAR), scale (room-scale to multi-km scale), topology (open-fields to complex mazes), dynamics (smoke, debris, sensorimotor failures and others) and tasks (from simple 2D coverage to foraging-inspired well-alternation tasks). We compare reinforcement learning baselines with a simple engineered robotics stack and a human player on 8 example worlds which show how different difficulty axes affect existing methods. Our results show that, when sensing is simplified to 2D, learned policies can perform multi-object search and well-alternation tasks surprisingly well in simple topologies, but they fall short of human performance in larger or more complex-topology environments where map-based baselines perform well, suggesting that map-based reasoning is the bottleneck in these scenarios.

papers.title: CIS-Transolver: A Cross-Layer Incremental-State Neural Operator for Fine-Scale Automotive Aerodynamic Flow Prediction
papers.abstract: Neural operators offer an efficient data-driven approach to rapid prediction of complex automotive aerodynamic flows. However, spectral bias and other factors limit accurate reconstruction of fine-scale flow variations near complex geometries. Existing studies improve the representation and fitting of fine-scale information mainly through information extraction and training objectives. Further study is needed to determine how extracted local details can be used continually in subsequent operator computations and contribute effectively to the overall flow-field representation. We propose CIS-Transolver, a cross-layer incremental-state neural operator that extends fine-scale modeling from local information extraction to its use across layers. The method extracts fine-scale information through local multiscale analysis and encodes it as geometric moment states that are propagated and updated across layers. By combining information from previous layers with feedback to the value representations in Physics-Attention, the method allows local details to contribute continually to subsequent modeling of global physical correlations. We systematically evaluate CIS-Transolver on three public automotive aerodynamics benchmarks, ShapeNet-Car, AhmedML, and DrivAerNet++, covering surface pressure fields and volumetric pressure and velocity fields. CIS-Transolver achieves the lowest mean relative L2 error among the evaluated methods for all five prediction metrics across the three benchmarks. The relative error reductions average 8.72% across the five metrics compared with the best baseline for each metric, reaching 16.38% for ShapeNet-Car pressure prediction and 15.60% for AhmedML velocity prediction. These results provide a new approach to fine-scale flow prediction for complex geometries.

papers.title: K-AoI: A Spatio-Temporal Synchronization Metric for Digital Twin-based Teleoperation in Dynamic Network Environments
papers.abstract: Synchronization between a digital twin (DT) and its physical robot is critical for effective teleoperation, as mismatches directly degrade operator awareness and task performance. Existing synchronization metrics are predominantly time-based and rarely capture the spatial consequences of delayed information during motion. In this paper, we introduce Kinematic Age of Information (K-AoI), a spatio-temporal metric that weights AoI by instantaneous Cartesian velocity, translating temporal staleness into physically meaningful spatial divergence. We implement and evaluate K-AoI on a DT teleoperation testbed comprising a six-degrees-of-freedom (6-DOF) manipulator, a Unity-based twin, and controlled network impairments using tc netem across seven network conditions. Per-sample analysis shows that K-AoI exhibits rank-correlations with AoI at $ρ\leq 0.65$ across all networks, dropping to $ρ= 0.22$ under satellite connections. This shows that K-AoI is not a simple transformation of AoI, but instead captures velocity-dependent degradation effects that time-only metrics cannot resolve. We further analyze AoI tail behavior using Ultra-Low AoI (ULAoI) and find that the commonly assumed Generalized Pareto Distribution (GPD) model is rejected. This reflects the impact of deterministic forwarding and bounded jitter, which violate standard extreme-value assumptions. Overall, K-AoI provides a complementary and physically grounded synchronization metric, linking network delay to task-relevant spatial error in digital-twin teleoperation systems. The dataset and testbed software are publicly available at: https://github.com/luziyaotian/kaoi-testbed.

papers.abstract: Passive-wheel quadrupedal robots offer energy-efficient locomotion through leg-driven propulsion and momentum-driven gliding. However, navigation requires coordinating steering with intermittent propulsion and adapting push-glide timing to task demands. Velocity-tracking objectives may suppress the speed variations inherent in skating, discouraging efficient gliding. To address these challenges, we propose SkateNav, a unified skating-navigation framework based on reinforcement learning. A time-budgeted goal-reaching objective allows the policy to jointly learn steering, propulsion, and their temporal allocation. An adaptive skating cycle structures gliding, pushing, and recovery, while frequency modulation at every control step adjusts phase durations to navigation demands. Simulation experiments demonstrate higher average success rates and lower cost of transport than the evaluated planner-controller baselines, with ablations confirming the contributions of cycle structure and frequency adaptation. Real-world experiments demonstrate zero-shot transfer from simulation to a passive-wheel Mini Cheetah across cluttered indoor spaces, slopes, and paved outdoor surfaces. Supplementary videos are available on the project page: https://ktw1404.github.io/SkateNav/

papers.title: EmbodiedWorld-200K: Toward Embodied World Agents via Embodied-Planning Dataset and Interactive World Models
papers.abstract: Building embodied agents that can perceive, reason, and act across diverse 3D worlds is a central research direction toward artificial general intelligence. Yet most existing work remains confined to specific tasks in a single scene and transfers poorly to new environments, leaving general embodied agents for open-world settings under-explored. We refer to such agents as Embodied World Agents (EWAs), whose defining property is the ability to understand diverse visual environments and execute general actions in open-world conditions. To advance EWA research, we study open-world embodied navigation-planning and release EmbodiedWorld-200K, a large-scale dataset of over 200K samples spanning diverse scenes. Each example is equipped with multi-level annotations, ranging from low-level camera-motion trajectories to high-level semantic instructions. The dataset also provides unified evaluation splits and task-specific metrics, supporting offline pretraining and fair evaluation of EWAs. Beyond offline supervision, a defining characteristic of an EWA is its interaction with the environment; training solely on offline data is therefore insufficient, especially for generalizing to scenes not covered in the training distribution. Building dedicated real interactive environments, however, is often prohibitively expensive. To address this, we propose a novel training scheme that employs a video world model as a low-cost environment proxy and performs interactive reinforcement-learning (RL) post-training of the EWA within it. Empirically, pretraining on EmbodiedWorld-200K substantially improves the open-world embodied planning ability of the EWA, and further RL post-training inside a world model yields clear gains on out-of-distribution scenes. The dataset, baseline checkpoints, and training and evaluation code are available at https://xiaokunfeng.github.io/EmbodiedWorld-200K/.

papers.title: Policy Search in Code Space for Multi-Agent Pathfinding
papers.abstract: Developing coordination policies for complex multi-agent systems relies on either labor-intensive algorithm design or opaque task-specific reinforcement learning. With recent advances in autonomous coding agents, we show that policy search directly in code space offers a compelling third path that combines automated optimization with explicit interpretability. We investigate a human-directed workflow in which coding agents iteratively propose, implement, evaluate, diagnose, and eventually refine algorithms guided by simulation feedback and explicit correctness verification. We conducted two case studies and found that this workflow robustly outperformed any manually engineered solutions. On a challenging map in the 2024 League of Robot Runners competition, a two-day search discovered a policy that exceeds the stronger locally reproduced competition entry by 35.0% on the densest instance and generalizes to unseen map instances. In simulated real-world warehouses with irregular lanes, continuous robot geometry, and asynchronous motion, a week-long search discovered an entirely new class of multi-agent pathfinding algorithm that outperforms a calibrated proprietary solution in throughput by 58.9%. Under stated assumptions, we further prove that the new algorithm is collision-free and completes, in finite time, every accepted goal that is not withdrawn or replaced. Together, the studies show that policy search in code space powered by state-of-the-art coding agents offers a highly competitive path to building real engineering solutions that are both effective and analytically tractable.

papers.title: Long-Horizon Multi-Object Rearrangement via Distilled Tree Search over Continuous Actions
papers.abstract: Despite recent advances in policy learning, long-horizon manipulation remains difficult because learned policies must avoid compounding errors while preserving future feasibility. While search-based planning can explicitly reason over such future consequences, it quickly becomes expensive in high-dimensional continuous action spaces. This raises a central question: how can long-horizon reasoning from search be transferred into policies in continuous action spaces? To this end, we propose DISCO: Distilled Tree Search over Continuous Actions. DISCO uses progressive-widening MCTS in physics simulation to generate long-horizon plans. During search, a learned policy proposes continuous actions, while a learned value function scores actions by their expected progress toward task completion. Using GPU-parallelized simulation, DISCO periodically distills MCTS-generated plans into the policy-value model, improving the action proposals and value estimates used in subsequent searches. Finally, the learned policy-value model can be directly deployed without the need for simulator-based search at test time. Across simulated and real-world rearrangement tasks, DISCO outperforms behavior cloning, reinforcement learning, and search-based baselines.

papers.title: ActTime: Action-Conditioned World Modeling for Time Series
papers.abstract: Time-series models increasingly condition on known future inputs. In controlled systems, some of these inputs are actions that can be changed, compared, and optimized before execution. A model must therefore do more than predict the realized future: it must predict how outcomes change under different actions from the same observed history and support reliable comparison of candidate plans. We introduce ActTime, an action-conditioned world model for time series. Over the observed history, ActTime updates variable-specific latent states through an action-conditioned transition and corrects them using observations. It then rolls the same transition forward under candidate actions to generate future trajectories. Training uses only factual trajectories, without paired alternative-action outcomes or planning supervision. We construct a simulator-grounded evaluation suite across building energy, traffic, greenhouse climate, and inventory management, covering factual prediction, intervention-effect prediction, offline decision making, and closed-loop planning. ActTime ranks first in 12 of 16 domain-task settings. Across eight methods, the mean pairwise model-ranking reversal rate is 17.8% between factual prediction and intervention fidelity, and rises to 28.4% between intervention fidelity and decision ranking. These results show that factual accuracy, intervention fidelity, and decision quality are related but not interchangeable.

papers.title: Frechet Forcing: Training Long-Horizon Streaming World Models from Short Clips
papers.abstract: Streaming video world models generate the future chunk by chunk, conditioned on their own past and a stream of actions. Trained on short clips, they drift once a rollout exceeds the training horizon, as prediction errors re-enter the context and compound. A common remedy is to train the model on its own rollouts via distribution matching distillation (DMD). For action-conditioned world models, the teacher becomes a bottleneck: an external video model is agnostic to the actions, whereas the model's own pretrained network drifts in the same manner as the student. We observe that a long rollout need not match a teacher, provided it remains a realistic continuation of its own scene that follows the commanded actions. Realism and scene fidelity can be measured against real-data statistics, which remain valid at any horizon, while action following is preserved by the model's conditional generation loss. We propose Fréchet Forcing, which fine-tunes a world model together with its deployed multi-step sampler under three constraints. Generative anchoring applies the flow-matching loss after a self-generated history ending on real data. Context fidelity, a Fréchet distance (FD) on latent statistics of the free rollout centred on each clip's own ground truth, keeps every rollout faithful to its scene. Reality matching, an FD to real frames in a frozen perceptual space, keeps the generated frames realistic. Because all three targets are derived from short real clips without comparing a rollout against a long recorded future, training requires no teacher, no online critic and no long videos. Fine-tuning MiniWorld-1B, pretrained on 253-frame clips, for at most 36 GPU-hours on 381-frame clips yields rollouts that remain stable beyond 4,000 frames and continue to follow their actions in both robot manipulation and camera-controlled exploration.

papers.abstract: Humanoid robots are envisioned to perform diverse human-level tasks through their anthropomorphic morphology. Their dual-arm configuration enables a broad range of everyday actions. Yet, as in humans, this morphology can constrain loco-manipulation when both arms are occupied or additional contacts are required beyond their reach. Supernumerary robotic limbs (SRLs) offer a way to extend these capabilities, but their integration requires the added limb to be coordinated with whole-body motion and balance. In this study, we develop and integrate a supernumerary arm into a humanoid platform to investigate how morphological augmentation reshapes its feasible action space. Through quantitative analysis and hardware experiments across two configurations, we show how the additional limb expands whole-body interaction capabilities by enabling manipulation and support to be coordinated beyond the constraints of the native dual-arm configuration. To control this augmented morphology, we leverage model-based trajectory optimization (TO) to generate dynamically feasible motions for goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (RL) controllers. The controllers are trained in simulation and transferred to hardware in a zero-shot manner, enabling coordinated whole-body skills for contact-rich tri-arm loco-manipulation. We further show vision-guided autonomous execution on selected tasks using diffusion policies trained from hardware demonstrations. Our findings suggest that humanoid morphology need not be restricted to human-like forms, but can be reimagined as an extensible design space for robotic augmentation.

Whereas most vector quantization uses Euclidean distance, we use a novel estimator of the first-passage-time as a quasi-metric, which aligns the planning abstraction with the controller's capabilities. We evaluate on the physical robot manipulation of the Tower of Hanoi puzzle: whereas existing state-of-the-art foundation models (VLAs, WAMs) only succeed when the solution trace in their training dataset, our method achieves 100\% success rate with only short-play data, demonstrate its ability to compose long-horizon solutions beyond the short demonstrated trajectories and execute them reliably. Our solution also outperforms strongest world-models by 13.3--85.3 percentage points on simulation benchmarks spanning manipulation and locomotion, demonstrating consistent progress and new capabilities.

papers.abstract: Objective. To perform a comparative biomechanical evaluation of NeO and ATID dental implant designs using finite element analysis and to determine the implant design providing the most favorable distribution of functional loading in cortical and cancellous bone. Materials and methods. A three-dimensional finite element model of a mandibular segment was reconstructed from computed tomography data. Two AlphaBio (Israel) dental implant designs, NeO and ATID, were analyzed. Equivalent von Mises stress distribution in cortical and cancellous bone was evaluated under vertical and horizontal loading ranging from 60 to 420 N, including physiological masticatory loading of 300 N. Results. Under a vertical load of 300 N, the NeO implant demonstrated lower maximum equivalent stresses than the ATID implant. In cortical bone, the maximum stress reached 16.5 MPa, which was 29.2% lower than that observed for the ATID implant. In cancellous bone, the maximum stress decreased to 2.2 MPa, representing a 64.5% reduction compared with the ATID design. A linear relationship was observed between the applied load and the equivalent von Mises stress. The NeO implant exhibited a more uniform stress distribution and lower stress concentration within the periimplant bone. Conclusions. Finite element analysis is an effective method for the biomechanical evaluation of dental implant systems. The NeO implant design provides a more favorable stress distribution than the ATID design, creating improved conditions for primary stability and osseointegration. These findings support the clinical use of the NeO implant, particularly in patients with reduced bone mineral density.

papers.title: Granular hydrogel bioink for macroporous pancreatic spheroid scaffolds
papers.abstract: Abstract Cells positioned more than several hundred microns away from a vascular network experience insufficient oxygen and nutrient supply due to diffusion limitations, leading to compromised viability and impaired function. This challenge is especially relevant in large, engineered 3D constructs which exceed the diffusion limitation of 100 - 200 µm, resulting in necrotic cores. Granular hydrogels have emerged as a promising approach for tissue engineering due to their inherent porosity. Their interconnected pores can facilitate mass transport of oxygen and nutrients, and therefore support cellular function. In this work, we developed a facile method to prepare bioprintable granular hydrogel bioink containing microparticles with tunable diameters, that can form porous scaffolds with different pore sizes and porosities. The bioink remained shelf-stable for at least 60 days when stored at 4 °C, as determined by the melt temperature. The macroporous granular hydrogel scaffold has inherent void spaces between the hydrogel microparticles, in which spheroids can be embedded. Pancreatic spheroids incorporated into the scaffold showed improved viability compared to free spheroids, indicating the granular microenvironment supports spheroid survival. Furthermore, functional studies of embedded pancreatic spheroids with glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) demonstrated preserved insulin secretion functionality. Our approach thus serves as a tunable platform for supporting the culture of functional spheroids and organoids, that has potential regenerative medicine applications in restoration of physiological functions when implanted.

papers.title: Machine Learning−Enabled Probabilistic Digital Twin for Halftone-Encoded Programmable Mechanical Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Abstract Programmable mechanical heterogeneity provides a powerful strategy for tailoring deformation behavior in architected materials. However, establishing predictive relationships between encoded material distributions and mechanical response remains challenging due to complex, nonlinear deformation. Here, we present a machine learning−enabled probabilistic digital twin for halftone-encoded architected materials fabricated via a binary, single-resin additive manufacturing approach. Specimens with systematically varied stiff domain fractions (0−50%) are subjected to uniaxial tensile loading, and deformation morphologies at large strain (60%) are used as input to a convolutional neural network, achieving a classification accuracy of 0.918 ± 0.046. Misclassifications occur primarily between adjacent stiffness states, consistent with the gradual variation in deformation morphology across the mechanical design space. To enable continuous prediction, classification outputs are reformulated through a probabilistic inference framework, where softmax probabilities are interpreted as distributions and converted into continuous estimates via probability-weighted averaging. Validation using four unseen specimens with an intermediate stiffness fraction of 25% provides a proof-of-concept demonstration of prediction at an unseen intermediate state, with estimates remaining within physically meaningful neighboring intervals. This approach establishes deformation morphology as a physically informative descriptor of encoded mechanical heterogeneity, enabling rapid, non-destructive prediction without constitutive modeling or finite element analysis. The framework provides a scalable pathway for integrating additive manufacturing, image-based mechanical testing, and data-driven modeling for the design and evaluation of architected materials.

papers.title: Development of montmorillonite-based 3D bio-printable bioink for bone tissue engineering
papers.abstract: The development of bioinks with optimal printability, mechanical stability, and biocompatibility is critical for advancing bone tissue engineering. In this study, we present a Montmorillonite-based 3D bio-printable bioink formulated using gelatin, low-methoxy pectin, and Montmorillonite K10 (MMT). The bioink was systematically optimized for its rheological properties, printability, and cross‑linking efficiency using calcium chloride and glutaraldehyde. Rheological assessments confirmed a shear-thinning behavior, facilitating smooth extrusion during bioprinting, while the viscoelastic analyses indicated a formulation-dependent balance between structural integrity and flexibility. Mechanical testing revealed that incorporation of MMT significantly enhanced the tensile strength and compressibility, essential for maintaining scaffold stability post-printing. Degradation studies further demonstrated the integrity of scaffolds over 28 days, with a controlled degradation profile, suitable for tissue integration. Biocompatibility was evaluated using Alamar Blue cytotoxicity assay and confocal imaging of hFOB 1.19 osteoblasts, which confirmed a high cell viability and progressive proliferation over seven days. SEM analysis highlighted a porous microarchitecture conducive to cell attachment and nutrient diffusion. The swelling behavior of the scaffolds indicated sufficient fluid retention to support long-term cell culture. Overall, the formulated bioink exhibited excellent printability, mechanical robustness, and cytocompatibility, making it a promising candidate for 3D bioprinted bone scaffolds. These findings provide a foundation for further investigations about in vivo performance, paving the way for its potential application in regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Optimization and prediction of process parameters in laser powder bed fusion of Ti-6Al-4V alloy using hybrid Taguchi-grey relational analysis and artificial neural network
papers.abstract: This study investigates the optimization and prediction of arithmetic average roughness (Ra) and hole dimensional accuracy of implant plates fabricated from Ti-6Al-4V alloy using laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF). Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) and an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) were employed to optimize the process parameters and predict the corresponding responses. The investigated process parameters were laser power (175, 185 and 195 W (W)), scanning speed (600, 900 and 1200 mm per second (mm/s)) and hatch distance (70, 90 and 110 μm (μm)). A Taguchi L9 orthogonal array was used to design the experiments. The responses considered were top flat surface roughness (TFSR), internal circular curve roughness (ICCR), external hole diameter (EHD), internal hole diameter (IHD) and volumetric energy density (VED). The GRA identified the optimum combination as a laser power of 175 W, scanning speed of 1200 mm/s, and hatch distance of 70 μm. An experiment conducted using these optimum parameters produced response values of 3.25 μm, 15.58 μm, 0.2767 mm (mm), 0.3093 mm and 53.26 J per cubic millimeter (J/mm 3 ), respectively. The ANN predicted corresponding values of 3.32 μm, 16.12 μm, 0.2834 mm, 0.3176 mm and 55.08 J/mm 3 , respectively. The prediction errors were below 3.5%, demonstrating good agreement between the experimental and predicted results. The findings confirm that the hybrid GRA and ANN approach is effective for optimizing process parameters and predicting Ra and hole dimensional characteristics in L-PBF of Ti-6Al-4V alloy.

papers.abstract: Fifth metacarpal shaft fractures account for a large share of hand trauma and often require operative internal fixation, yet conventional dorsal plates and cannulated screws present a stiffness mismatch with native bone and the insertion of screws can shear surface coatings. This study presents the design, fabrication, and preliminary characterisation of a low-profile, BaTiO3-coated dorsal fixation plate prototype for the fifth metacarpal bone. A curved, 0.5 mm plate was modelled in SolidWorks and overlaid with a randomised Delaunay lattice in Meshmixer, achieving 73.6% porosity with a 70% mesh reduction strategy. A linear static finite element study of a simplified periodic surrogate of the plate (nominal polymer properties, 300 N load) is reported only as an illustrative response, not as evidence of mechanical suitability. Plates were manufactured by masked stereolithography in a water-washable resin not intended for implantation (not MED610), with an average accuracy of 98.77% on three features measured before coating; the dimensions after the 120 °C and 180 °C coating steps were not remeasured. A barium titanate precursor was synthesised via the propionate route and deposited through a three-cycle, low-temperature (120 °C) submersion process followed by a solvothermal treatment at 180 °C for 1 h. Optical microscopy and SEM/EDS showed qualitative surface coverage with barium and titanium and open pores, and XRD showed reflections consistent with perovskite BaTiO3; the polymorph, thickness, adhesion, uniformity and mechanical stability of the coating were not quantified. Under cyclic compressive loading (1–2 N), a coated plate dried at 120 °C, before the solvothermal step was introduced, generated an alternating open-circuit voltage of 0.62 ± 0.08 V at 1 N and 0.93 ± 0.10 V at 2 N (peak-to-peak), much larger than that of an uncoated plate; its origin remains to be established. This is a fabrication and preliminary characterisation study of a non-biocompatible prototype: mechanical testing of the printed structure, poled and replicate electrical measurements, and biological evaluation have not yet been performed and are the next steps.

papers.title: Periprosthetic Femoral Fracture in Hip Arthroplasty Using Cemented Stems: Toward a Construct-Level and Time-Dependent Perspective
papers.abstract: Periprosthetic femoral fracture (PFF) is an increasingly recognized complication following cemented total hip arthroplasty (THA); it is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality and often occurring several years after implantation. Although polished taper-slip (PTS) stems demonstrate favorable long-term survivorship, they have also been associated with a higher incidence of PFF, the biomechanical basis of which remains unclear. Existing studies have investigated a few key aspects of cemented THA, including implant migration, cement behavior, and fracture biomechanics. However, these factors are typically examined in isolation or under simplified conditions, and current construct-level models evaluate fracture without accounting for prior loading history. Pre-clinical testing standards relevant to fracture in cemented THA remain limited, with existing standards addressing individual components under simplified laboratory conditions rather than the integrated periprosthetic system under a physiologically relevant environment. As a result, how the implant–cement–bone construct evolves from implantation to eventual failure remains insufficiently characterized. In this study, we critically evaluate current experimental approaches and identify the absence of a time-resolved, construct-level framework as a key limitation. We outline a conceptual framework describing how implant migration, material response, and fracture behavior evolve with loading exposure. This framework may provide a foundation for both improving the mechanistic understanding of PFF and supporting the development of future pre-clinical testing strategies that can better reflect clinical loading conditions.

papers.title: Hybrid analytical-deep learning framework for fractional multi-temperature thermo-mechanical damage analysis in hollow cylinders with temperature-dependent heat conduction
papers.abstract: This study develops a unified analytical–computational framework for transient heat transfer and irreversible thermo-mechanical damage in a hollow cylinder subjected to thermal shock. Caputo fractional thermal memory, multi-temperature nonequilibrium transport, exponential temperature-dependent conductivity, and history-dependent continuum damage are coupled through an incremental scheme. At each increment, the current damage state is fixed during the double-Laplace thermoelastic solution, physical temperatures are reconstructed only after numerical inversion and inverse Kirchhoff transformation, and the nondecreasing history variable is subsequently updated. The novelty lies in integrating these mechanisms with damage-consistent mechanics, independent finite-element verification, and leakage-free surrogate acceleration within one framework. COMSOL verification gives relative L 2 errors of 0.62%, 0.94%, 0.81%, and 1.18% for conductive temperature, mean stress, volumetric strain, and damage, respectively, with final mesh variation of 0.33%. Results show that fractional thermal memory governs thermal penetration, energy localization, stress redistribution, entropy generation, and damage evolution, while variable conductivity alters heat diffusion and stress localization. On genuinely unseen operating conditions, the supervised mechanics-informed neural-network surrogate achieves R 2 = 0.9983 ± 0.0004 and RMSE = 0.0021 ± 0.0002, whereas DeepONet reaches R 2 = 0.9991 ± 0.0002 and RMSE = 0.0015 ± 0.0001. Ablation reduces R 2 to 0.979 when fractional memory is removed, confirming its dominant contribution. Prediction time decreases from 21.8 s analytically and 43.6 s by finite elements to 0.078 s for MNN and 0.021 s for DeepONet, enabling rapid damage-aware thermal assessment and design. The framework also predicts conductive and thermodynamic temperatures, displacement, stresses, volumetric strain, strain-energy density, entropy generation, and progressive damage, providing interpretable fields for severe thermal environments.

papers.abstract: The growing number of arthroplasties is linked to a rise in implant failures, with aseptic loosening being a significant factor in the need for revision surgeries. The long-term success of titanium implants regarding robust osseointegration depends not only on osteoblast-driven bone formation, but also on a balanced osteoimmune process, linking implant surface cues to coordinated bone remodelling. Using electrical discharge machining (EDM) and diamond-like carbon (DLC) as exemplars of topographical and physicochemical surface-engineering strategies, this review summarizes their generated surface cues and discusses how these cues may influence protein adsorption, osteoblast behaviour, macrophage activation, osteoclastogenesis, and bone-remodelling outcomes. Current evidence remains largely focused on osteogenic endpoints, whereas macrophage and osteoclast-specific data are still scarce. We therefore re-evaluate EDM and DLC surface modifications through an osteoimmunology framework and propose that future studies incorporate immune cell and remodelling-linked endpoints, as well as combined EDM/DLC interfaces, to support rational surface design for durable osseointegration.

papers.abstract: This study proposes a unified physics-informed machine-learning (PIML) framework for predicting the dynamic responses of traction motor housings under unseen geometric conditions. The framework incorporates three key forms of physical priors into a neural network. First, an observation bias is introduced through modal coordinate encoding, which embeds both geometric characteristics and excitation-dependent modal contributions into the neural network. Second, an inductive bias is incorporated by deploying a separable deep operator network architecture, which effectively learns nonlinear operator mappings and generalizes them to unseen housing geometries. Third, a learning bias is enforced by embedding the governing equations of structural dynamics into the training process to ensure physically consistent predictions. Novel training strategies are also employed to enhance convergence and numerical stability during physics-informed training. Quantitative evaluations and ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, achieving a mean MAPE of 3.32 % across the full test set and outperforming conventional neural networks. A design-optimization application further confirms that the proposed framework improves computational efficiency compared with conventional finite element analysis. Overall, this study establishes a robust framework for accelerating AI-driven design optimization and advancing intelligent structural engineering methodologies.

The rectangular diaphragm design can be changed to smooth the transition between normal and touch modes and produce more consistent linearity and sensitivity. Numerical computation, FEA simulation and deep neural network (DNN) surrogate model for predicting the performance characteristics of a novel MEMS capacitive pressure sensor. A comprehensive dataset is constructed by combining Numerical computation and FEA-simulated results across a wide range of diaphragm geometries and applied pressure conditions. A DNN surrogate model is subsequently developed and trained on this dataset to predict the performance characteristics of the proposed MEMS capacitive pressure sensor. papers.title: Sensitivity-driven model updating for bridge structures using operational modal analysis and enhanced batched Thompson sampling-based Bayesian optimization
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a robust and effective finite element model updating (FEMU) framework for inverse parameter identification of bridge structures by integrating operational modal analysis (OMA) and variance-based global sensitivity analysis (GSA) with an enhanced batched Thompson sampling-based Bayesian optimization (ETS-BO) method. Specifically, a Gaussian process (GP) model is constructed to approximate the nonlinear relationship between uncertain structural parameters and the corresponding modal responses. Leveraging the trained GP model, the variance-based GSA identifies the most influential parameters governing the dynamic behavior of the bridge, thereby significantly reducing the dimensionality of the FEMU problem and improving computational efficiency. Building upon the reduced parameter space, the ETS-BO method is developed by integrating an adaptive trust-region selection strategy with an enhanced batched Thompson sampling (ETS) method to efficiently solve the FEMU problem. The adaptive trust-region selection evaluates the improvement potential at the regional level, guiding the search toward promising regions of the parameter space while avoiding over-exploration of less promising ones. The trust region method is then applied to perform local optimization, whereby each trust region is adaptively expanded or contracted based on its observed improvement history, and local optimization runs exhibiting greater potential for further improvement are selectively continued. Within the selected trust regions, the ETS method is employed to determine the optimal updating parameters by iteratively selecting batches of candidate solutions sampled from the posterior distributions of the corresponding independent GP models. The effectiveness of the proposed ETS-BO is validated through a real-world case study of a bridge structure equipped with wireless accelerometers for vibration monitoring. Ambient vibration responses recorded under normal traffic conditions are analyzed using OMA to identify modal parameters, which subsequently serve as targets for updating the finite element (FE) model developed to represent the structural behavior of the bridge. The results demonstrate that the proposed ETS-BO requires substantially fewer FE evaluations than conventional optimization methods while achieving rapid convergence toward the optimal solution. Furthermore, the updated FE model closely reproduces the experimentally identified modal parameters, including natural frequencies and mode shape correlations, thereby providing a reliable numerical representation of the in-service dynamic behavior of the bridge and demonstrating the potential of the proposed framework to support long-term structural health monitoring of large-scale civil infrastructure systems.

papers.title: Improving the interfacial bonding strength of CuCrZr/316L multi-material during laser powder bed fusion by scanning strategies
papers.abstract: Copper/steel multi-material components integrate structural load-bearing capability with thermoelectric functionality, offering significant potential for operation under extreme service conditions. However, the discrepancies in physical properties between materials promote crack formation at the interface of copper/steel multi-materials, which significantly degrades their service performance. In this paper, we investigate the effects of interlayer design combined with laser remelting on the evolution of residual stress and mechanical properties of CuCrZr/316L multi-material manufactured by Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF). The surface morphology, element distribution, microhardness, tensile properties, and microstructure of the CuCrZr/316L multi-material interface are analyzed. The results reveal that the laser remelting scanning strategy significantly diminishes residual stress at the CuCrZr/316L multi-material interface. The combination of 90° rotational remelting for 316L and 180° remelting for CuCrZr shows the lowest interfacial stress level, with the maximum value not exceeding the yield strength of 316L. The ultimate tensile strengths of the vertically and horizontally integrated CuCrZr/316L multi-material are 324.3 ± 1.9 MPa and 534.1 ± 3.4 MPa, respectively. In addition, the fracture of vertically bonded specimens occurred in the CuCrZr region, with clear evidence of necking. The fusion zone shows the highest microhardness among all samples, with an average microhardness of 177.64 ± 12.04 HV. The findings of the research provide valuable scanning strategies for enhancing the mechanical properties of copper/steel multi-materials and support the reliable fabrication of high-performance multi-material components.

papers.title: Multi-Objective Optimization of SLM Parameters for SS316L: Surface Quality, Microhardness, and Tribological Assessment
papers.abstract: Austenitic stainless steel 316L (SS316L) is used in orthopedic and dental implants, surgical instruments, and aerospace fluid-handling components because of its corrosion resistance and ductility. Selective Laser Melting (SLM) produces these parts with internal channels that casting and machining cannot deliver. However, as-built SS316L surfaces contain spatter, partially fused powder, and near-surface porosity that raise roughness and reduce fatigue strength, corrosion resistance, and wear performance. Producing parts that meet both surface and mechanical requirements in a single build remains difficult. This study examines how laser power, scanning speed, layer thickness, and hatch spacing affect the surface roughness, microhardness, and wear of SLM-fabricated SS316L. A Box–Behnken Design under Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was used for 27 experimental trials. Surface roughness was measured by stylus profilometry, microhardness by Vickers indentation, and dry sliding wear with a block-on-disc tribometer. Regression analysis and multi-response desirability optimization were carried out in Minitab. Processing parameters showed clear effects on surface quality and hardness; the wear response varied considerably because of localized surface defects and particle adhesion. Multi-objective optimization gave a composite desirability of 0.7603 at 260.6 W, 507.1 mm/s, 41.9 μm, and 120.0 μm. The predicted upper surface roughness, side surface roughness, and microhardness were 5.74 μm, 13.63 μm, and 210.39 HV, respectively. Run 26, tested at a volumetric energy density (VED) of 125.0 J/mm3, recorded an upper surface roughness of 5.48 μm and a microhardness of 218.1 HV. Surface defects strongly influenced the sliding response. The study provides a practical RSM-based route for selecting SLM parameters that balance surface quality and microhardness in SS316L components.

papers.title: Extrusion‐Based Bioprinting of Living Bioinks for Tissue and Organ Engineering
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Recapitulating the structural complexity of native tissues is a central challenge in tissue engineering, as tissue architecture critically influences cellular maturation and physiological function. Among 3D bioprinting technologies, extrusion‐based bioprinting (EBB) has emerged as the predominant platform for fabricating complex, heterogeneous, and large‐scale tissues, despite inherent limitations in printing speed and resolution. In this review, we examine the defining advantage underlying EBB's widespread adoption: its exceptional versatility. We discuss the broad range of living bioinks and biomaterial inks compatible with extrusion, emphasizing the ease with which multiple materials and cell populations can be integrated within a single construct. We then examine how support matrices and advanced printhead geometries have expanded the accessible material and architectural space, enabling the fabrication of soft, freeform, anisotropic, and multicompartment tissues. We critically evaluate the fundamental physical constraints of extrusion, particularly the tradeoff between printing resolution and cell‐damaging shear stress, and highlight strategies that transform these limitations into new biofabrication capabilities. Finally, we identify 4D bioprinting, high‐speed fabrication, and in situ bioprinting as three emerging frontiers that may define the next generation of EBB for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Multi-objective optimization of subsea U-shaped metal seals using a surrogate model and NSGA-II
papers.abstract: The U-shaped metal seal ring of the subsea tubing hanger is a critical component ensuring wellhead sealing integrity, with its sealing performance determining the safe operation of oil and gas production systems. Addressing the analytical challenges posed by the seal's multi-parameter and highly nonlinear characteristics, this study establishes an optimization method integrating Optimized Latin Hypercube Sampling (Opt-LHD), XGBoost surrogate modeling, and the multi-objective genetic algorithm (NSGA-II). Initially, Finite Element Analysis (FEA) is utilized to evaluate the stress distribution and contact behavior, elucidating the sealing mechanism. Opt-LHD is then employed to construct a high-coverage sample space. Two surrogate models—XGBoost and BP neural network—are established and compared for the U-shaped metal seal. Through cross-validation and error analysis, the XGBoost model, exhibiting superior generalization, is selected to replace time-consuming FEA. Subsequently, a dual-objective global optimization targeting increased maximum contact pressure and reduced maximum equivalent stress is performed using NSGA-II. The Pareto front is validated through FEA to determine the optimized design. Simulation results demonstrate that the optimized seal ring achieves a 10.07% increase in maximum contact pressure and an 8% reduction in maximum equivalent stress, simultaneously enhancing sealing performance and structural safety, thereby validating the effectiveness of this optimization methodology.

papers.title: An Integrated Structural Health Monitoring and Digital Twin Framework for Condition Assessment of Gravity Dams
papers.abstract: This study presents a Digital Twin-based Structural Health Monitoring framework for the assessment of existing concrete gravity dams. The proposed methodology integrates distributed sensing, automated signal processing, finite element modelling, model calibration and validation, degradation sensitivity analysis, and digital visualization within a unified monitoring framework. A network of inertial sensors is deployed along the dam to characterize its dynamic and quasi-static response. Hourly monitoring records are processed to identify natural frequencies using Fast Fourier Transform, Power Spectral Density, and Peak Picking techniques, while acceleration measurements are also used to derive displacement and inclination indicators. A 3D finite element model developed in ANSYS Mechanical APDL is calibrated by iteratively updating the effective Young’s modulus and density until the relative error between numerical and experimentally identified modal frequencies is below 5%. Independent validation using inclination measurements resulted in relative differences between 0.74% and 4.92%. The calibrated Digital Twin is subsequently used to simulate progressive stiffness degradation and establish relationships between degradation, modal properties, and structural deformation. The resulting model-informed thresholds are integrated into a digital monitoring platform for automated condition assessment and anomaly detection. The framework provides a physically interpretable approach for complementing conventional dam safety inspections with long-term quantitative structural health information.

papers.title: Development of montmorillonite-based 3D bio-printable bioink for bone tissue engineering
papers.abstract: The development of bioinks with optimal printability, mechanical stability, and biocompatibility is critical for advancing bone tissue engineering. In this study, we present a Montmorillonite-based 3D bio-printable bioink formulated using gelatin, low-methoxy pectin, and Montmorillonite K10 (MMT). The bioink was systematically optimized for its rheological properties, printability, and cross‑linking efficiency using calcium chloride and glutaraldehyde. Rheological assessments confirmed a shear-thinning behavior, facilitating smooth extrusion during bioprinting, while the viscoelastic analyses indicated a formulation-dependent balance between structural integrity and flexibility. Mechanical testing revealed that incorporation of MMT significantly enhanced the tensile strength and compressibility, essential for maintaining scaffold stability post-printing. Degradation studies further demonstrated the integrity of scaffolds over 28 days, with a controlled degradation profile, suitable for tissue integration. Biocompatibility was evaluated using Alamar Blue cytotoxicity assay and confocal imaging of hFOB 1.19 osteoblasts, which confirmed a high cell viability and progressive proliferation over seven days. SEM analysis highlighted a porous microarchitecture conducive to cell attachment and nutrient diffusion. The swelling behavior of the scaffolds indicated sufficient fluid retention to support long-term cell culture. Overall, the formulated bioink exhibited excellent printability, mechanical robustness, and cytocompatibility, making it a promising candidate for 3D bioprinted bone scaffolds. These findings provide a foundation for further investigations about in vivo performance, paving the way for its potential application in regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Versatile polyacrylamide/gum hybrid hydrogels for tunable mechanics and high-fidelity 3D extrusion printing
papers.abstract: Abstract Polyacrylamide (PAM) hydrogels are widely used in biological research for their well-established and tunable mechanical properties, which can closely match native tissue stiffness, making them attractive for mechanobiology, biosensing and tissue engineering. However, extrusion-based 3D printing of PAM remains challenging due to the inherently low viscosity of precursor solutions. Existing strategies reach printable viscosities with rheology modifiers such as Laponite clays or protein-based microgels, but these additives strongly couple printability to final stiffness, substantially increasing the elastic modulus and compromising the soft, tunable character that makes PAM valuable. Here, we present a novel yet accessible one-pot strategy for extrusion-printable PAM hydrogels, using natural polysaccharide gums as a distinct class of rheology modifier. Unlike conventional additives, gums confer the shear-thinning and viscoelastic structure required for extrusion at low concentrations (2–4 w/v %), while preserving the established AM/BIS-stiffness relationship and allowing modulus to be tuned independently through monomer concentration. Tragacanth, xanthan, and guar gums were systematically evaluated across concentrations for their effects on ink rheology, print fidelity, and mechanics. High-fidelity printing was achieved at concentrations as low as 2 w/v % for guar and 3 w/v % for tragacanth and xanthan. Mechanical characterization reveals soft, tunable properties, with elastic moduli from 5 to 58 kPa across gum type and concentration, spanning a broad range of soft tissue stiffnesses. Guar and tragacanth in particular produced moduli statistically comparable to pure PAM, confirming minimal impact on network mechanics. Preliminary cytocompatibility assays confirm these hybrid hydrogels support MDCK I cell viability. We further demonstrate core-shell extrusion printing of PAM/gum hydrogels for the first time, using a sacrificial core to generate hollow, perfusable channels down to ~200 µm in diameter. Together, these results establish PAM/gum hydrogels as a printable, mechanically tunable ink platform, laying a materials-processing foundation for architecturally complex, channeled PAM-based constructs.

papers.abstract: Mineralization and vascularization are essential processes for implant osseointegration around titanium, and insufficient surface bioactivity affects its clinical performance; thus, surface modification of implants is necessary. This study aimed to establish a sodium alginate/collagen/troxerutin coating on the surface of titanium to promote angiogenic and osteogenic ability. The results indicate that the material has satisfactory biocompatibility in terms of cell viability. Mouse embryonic osteoblast cells (MC3T3-E1) cells on the alginate/collagen/troxerutin coating significantly influenced mineralized nodule formation and Alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity. The alginate/collagen/troxerutin coating promoted tube formation and the migration of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). The alginate/collagen/troxerutin coating also resulted in increased osteogenic and angiogenic gene expression. In addition, more bone formation was observed in the Ti-alginate/collagen/troxerutin group than in the other groups in vivo . The combination of troxerutin with sodium alginate and collagen resulted in osteogenic and angiogenic effects. It offers a potential option for surface modification of implants and has good application prospects in the future.
