papers.title: Conventional to advanced techniques: Progress in titanium alloys for biomedical applications
papers.abstract: The biocompatibility, high strength-to-weight ratio, mechanical properties, and resistance to corrosion of titanium and its alloys, making them suitable for implants. The major factors influencing titanium implant performance depends on fabrication technique, microstruc­ture, resistance to corrosion, tribocorrosion, osseointegration and its stability. This review focuses the impact of conventional manufacturing technique such as welding, casting, powder metallurgy, forging, rolling, and extrusion and their effect on metal implants. To overcome the limitations of conventional techniques, further development of advanced manufacturing strategies capable of achieving complex geometries and tailored properties for next-generation biomedical implants. Specific focus is placed on powder bed fusion, directed energy deposition, material extrusion, binder jetting, and material jetting. The impact of processing technique on mechanical properties, microstructure, corrosion resistance and overall implant longevity is discussed. Furthermore, challenges such as the high elastic modulus of conventional Ti alloys, limited control over the strength, ductility, biocompatibility, surface degradation and tribocorrosion, and the need for adaptive and long-term implant monitoring continue to drive research toward integrated material, computational, manufacturing, and digital strategies. Emerging approaches such as high-entropy titanium alloys, artificial intelligence, machine learning, 4D printing, smart implant technologies, and digital twinning for predicting and controlling implant performance, are emphasised in this review. Their incorporation with additive manufacturing (AM) opens new possibilities for enhancing Ti implants, which can offer improved mechanical compatibility, corrosion resistance, wear resistance, personalized functionality, and consistent long-term performance.

papers.title: Effects of physiological and manipulative loading conditions on the sacroiliac joint: a three-dimensional finite element analysis
papers.abstract: Manual therapy is applied in the conservative management of sacroiliac joint (SIJ)-related symptoms, but whether its biomechanical effect is primarily related to joint mobilization or periarticular soft-tissue modulation remains unclear. This study compared the mechanical responses of the SIJ-iliolumbar ligament complex under four prescribed loading and constraint configurations: physiological compressive stress (PCS), traction manipulation stress (TMS), oblique-pulling manipulation (OPM), and counter-directional sacral thrust with iliac mobilization (CDST-IM) using three-dimensional finite element analysis. A CT-based lumbar spine-pelvis finite element model was reconstructed from computed tomography data of a healthy 31-year-old male volunteer. Four loading conditions were simulated: 300 N downward compression at L4, 300 N vertical traction at L4, 300 N traction combined with 10° posterior rotation of the right ilium, and 600 N posterior force applied to the right ilium along the SIJ direction. von Mises stress (VMS), Total Deformation (TD), and range of motion (ROM) of the SIJ, together with iliolumbar ligament VMS and TD, were evaluated. PCS and TMS showed little difference in the evaluated responses under bilateral iliac constraint. OPM generated the greatest cartilage VMS, cartilage TD, right SIJ ROM, and iliolumbar ligament TD, whereas CDST-IM produced a more moderate SIJ response with comparatively low ligament TD. On the right side, the surface showing greater cartilage TD changed from the sacral surface under PCS/TMS to the iliac surface under OPM/CDST-IM. These findings indicate limited SIJ micromotion and distinct ligament responses under the prescribed loading and constraint configurations.

papers.abstract: This study analyzed the impact of diabetes mellitus and smoking on early dental implant loss in patients undergoing oral bisphosphonate therapy, considering the combined influence of systemic, behavioral, and pharmacological factors on osseointegration. The research was conducted through a descriptive literature review with a qualitative approach, using studies addressing risk factors associated with dental implant failure. The results demonstrated that diabetes mellitus, particularly when associated with inadequate glycemic control, may impair healing, bone metabolism, and the initial stability of dental implants. Smoking also represents an important risk factor because it interferes with the biological conditions required for tissue repair and may contribute to peri-implant complications. Regarding oral bisphosphonates, their use requires individualized assessment considering treatment duration, therapeutic indication, systemic conditions, and other associated factors. The analysis showed that none of these conditions should be considered separately as a determining cause of early implant loss, since implant failure has a multifactorial nature. However, the association between uncontrolled diabetes, smoking, and bisphosphonate therapy may create a more complex clinical scenario requiring additional care. Positive aspects include the possibility of controlling modifiable factors, individualized treatment planning, and periodic follow-up. Areas requiring improvement include systematic risk assessment and further clinical studies investigating the simultaneous association of these conditions. It is concluded that detailed medical history assessment, metabolic control, smoking cessation guidance, medication history evaluation, and multidisciplinary follow-up are fundamental strategies for increasing the safety, predictability, and success of implant rehabilitation. The integration of scientific evidence with clinical practice contributes to safer therapeutic decisions and effective prevention of early implant failures.

papers.title: Closed-loop photoreactor design enabled by machine learning and digital twins
papers.abstract: Abstract Designing efficient photoreactors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of reflection, scattering, and absorption. Here, we introduce a closed-loop workflow integrating ray-tracing digital twins with multi-objective Bayesian optimization to design photoreactors with high photon capture and uniform irradiation. A digital 3D reactor model is calibrated using measured emission characteristics, reflectivity data, and geometrical properties and validated against potassium ferrioxalate actinometry. The validated model explores reflector shape and vial positioning, identifying geometries that maximize incident photon flux while maintaining homogeneity across 16 vials. Experimental validation using a photocatalytic Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling shows that reaction yields track simulated photon flux. The optimized reactor is further applied to quantum-yield screening, enabling mechanistic insights across diverse conditions in a single experiment. This work establishes an experimentally validated virtual co-design framework in which machine learning and digital twins accelerate photoreactor development and support quantitative understanding of photochemical processes.

papers.title: Imaging-derived coronary fractional flow reserve: advances in physics-based, machine learning, and physics-informed methods
papers.abstract: Purpose of Review: Imaging-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR) is rapidly evolving beyond conventional computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-based pipelines toward machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and physics-informed approaches that enable fast, wire-free, and scalable functional assessment of coronary artery stenosis. This review synthesizes recent advances in computed tomography (CT)- and angiography-based FFR measurement, with particular emphasis on emerging physics-informed neural networks and neural operators (PINNs and PINOs), as well as key considerations for their clinical translation. Recent Findings: ML/DL approaches have markedly improved automation and computational speed, enabling prediction of pressure and FFR from anatomical descriptors or angiographic contrast dynamics. However, their real-world performance and generalizability can remain variable and sensitive to domain shift, due to multi-center heterogeneity, interpretability challenges, and differences in acquisition protocols and image quality. Physics-informed learning introduces conservation structure and boundary-condition consistency into model training, improving generalizability and reducing dependence on dense supervision while maintaining rapid inference. Recent evaluation trends increasingly highlight deployment-oriented metrics, including calibration, uncertainty quantification, and quality-control gatekeeping, as essential for safe clinical use. Summary: The field is converging toward imaging-derived FFR methods that are faster, more automated, and more reliable. While ML/DL offers substantial efficiency gains, physics-informed frameworks such as PINNs and PINOs may provide a more robust balance between speed and physical consistency. Prospective multi-center validation and standardized evaluation will be critical to support broad and safe clinical adoption.

papers.title: TCL: Enabling Fast and Efficient Cross-Hardware Tensor Program Optimization via Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Deep learning (DL) compilers rely on cost models and auto-tuning to optimize tensor programs for target hardware. However, existing approaches depend on large offline datasets, incurring high collection costs and offering suboptimal transferability across platforms. In this paper, we introduce TCL , a novel efficient and transferable compiler framework for fast tensor program optimization across diverse hardware platforms to address these challenges. Specifically, TCL is built on three core enablers: (1) the RDU Sampler , a data-efficient active learning strategy that selects only 10% of tensor programs by jointly optimizing R epresentativeness, D iversity, and U ncertainty, substantially reducing data collection costs while maintaining near-original model accuracy; (2) a new Mamba-based cost model that efficiently captures long-range schedule dependencies while achieving a favorable trade-off between prediction accuracy and computational cost through reduced parameterization and lightweight sequence modeling; and (3) a continuous knowledge distillation framework that effectively and progressively transfers knowledge across multiple hardware platforms while avoiding the parameter explosion and data dependency issues typically caused by traditional multi-task learning. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of each individual enabler and the holistic TCL framework. When optimizing a range of mainstream DL models on both CPU and GPU platforms, TCL achieves, on average, 16.8 × and 12.48 × faster tuning time, and 1.20 × and 1.13 × lower inference latency, respectively, compared to Tenset-MLP.

papers.title: Multiobjective Optimization of Synthetically Accessible Homogeneous Catalysts Reveals Tradeoffs for Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
papers.abstract: Abstract The selective conversion of methane to methanol remains a major challenge in catalysis, and no earth-abundant homogeneous catalyst has been demonstrated to carry out this transformation with high turnover. To explore previously synthesized complexes that might be amenable for this transformation, we start from macrocyclic ligands from experimental structures in the Cambridge Structural Database. After expanding this set of ligands with Hammett-tuning functionalization, we construct a design space of 21.9 million Mn and Fe catalysts. We employ active learning using neural network surrogate models with quantified uncertainty to efficiently identify catalysts with optimal methane-to-methanol turnover. We do this by jointly optimizing density functional theory (DFT)-computed hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and methyl radical rebound energetics. Square planar tetraaza-based macrocycles in combination with low-spin Fe(II) or Mn(II) emerge as a privileged class of transition metal complexes within the Pareto-optimal set, with Mn(II) catalysts exhibiting balanced energetic tradeoffs of the two steps. In contrast, porphyrin catalysts exhibit favorable HAT but unfavorable rebound, and seesaw catalysts, which are not widely employed, are indeed the least favorable in our set. Full reaction coordinate analysis of representative Pareto-optimal catalysts reveals that HAT and rebound thermodynamics no longer govern turnover, which is instead determined by the stability of the metal–oxo intermediate and the rebound kinetic barrier. Nonetheless, the resulting energetic spans for these catalysts remain competitive with known earth-abundant, methane-to-methanol catalysts, underscoring the effectiveness of active learning for discovering previously unexplored, synthetically accessible catalysts and unraveling catalyst design principles for methane-to-methanol reactivity.

papers.title: Moiré strain skyrmions in sliding twisted bilayers
papers.abstract: Strain defect is crucial to the physical properties of solid materials. Among them, strain glass induced by defect engineering provides an important paradigm for nanoscale domain manipulation. Here, we propose purely mechanical moiré strain Skyrmions, a topologically protected elastic textures whose motion can be controlled by interlayer sliding and the chirality of the moiré bilayer. Using an empirical continuum elastic model combined with symmetry analysis, we demonstrate the Skyrmion lattice structure as the elastic ground state. Under interlayer sliding, these moiré strain Skyrmions exhibit the Skyrmion Hall effect of transverse motion, with a Hall angle determined by bilayer chirality and inversely proportional to the moiré twist angle. Our work establishes interlayer sliding as an efficient, low-energy control knob for topological excitations, offering a new paradigm for designing chiral-material-based information transport devices.

papers.title: rush: Scalable Asynchronous Distributed Computing via Shared State in R
papers.abstract: Many algorithms in statistics and machine learning can be parallelized in an asynchronous manner where workers need to communicate through shared state rather than execute independent tasks dispatched by a central controller. Especially in modern hyperparameter optimization and parallel black-box optimization with expensive objectives, this decentralized approach has become widespread, and several Python frameworks adopt it (e.g., Optuna, DeepHyper, and Hyperopt). However, all popular R packages for parallel computing follow a centralized controller-worker architecture that does not support this pattern. We present rush, an R package that provides a shared-state coordination layer for asynchronously parallelized iterative algorithms. rush uses a Redis database as a shared key-value store: workers read and write task data through the database and independently execute their own loops. The package provides a high-level API for managing tasks and their lifecycle, featuring sub-millisecond per-task overhead, robust error handling with automatic detection of lost workers, and efficient caching. rush optionally integrates with the mlr3 ecosystem, powering asynchronous optimization in the bbotk and mlr3tuning packages. We demonstrate the practical utility of rush by implementing asynchronous decentralized Bayesian optimization (ADBO) and benchmarking it on hyperparameter optimization of LightGBM across four datasets using 448 workers.

papers.title: Beyond constant error: Heteroscedastic Bayesian model combination for modeling unmeasured nuclei
papers.abstract: Experimentally inaccessible regions of the nuclear chart remain a challenge for global models of atomic nuclei to predict. This includes exotic nuclei near particle drip lines, superheavy elements at the extremes of mass and charge, and the neutron-rich pathways of astrophysical processes in explosive stellar environments where heavy elements are created. Given that individual nuclear models are imperfect, deep extrapolations are best approached using model ensembles, which allow for the systematic combination of diverse theoretical predictions. In this study, we employ the recently introduced Bayesian Model Combination (BMC) method, based on statistical machine learning, that provides robust uncertainty quantification for forecasts using model ensembles. To account for the inherent degradation of predictive power as models extrapolate into the yet-unexplored domain, we introduce a heteroscedastic BMC framework in which the combined theoretical uncertainty is treated as a dynamic quantity. We apply this methodology to an ensemble of realistic energy density functionals with a specific focus on the $Z=46\text{--}52$ isotopic chains. We rigorously validate the approach using both experimental data and synthetic data designed to assess performance in the deep extrapolation regime. Our results demonstrate that the proposed heteroscedastic approach yields superior calibration metrics and provides statistically principled assessments of the particle drip lines.

papers.title: yancc: A GPU-accelerated, differentiable solver for neoclassical transport in tokamaks and stellarators
papers.abstract: Abstract We present yancc, a new GPU-accelerated solver for the drift kinetic equation that computes neoclassical transport fluxes, flows, and currents in tokamaks and stellarators. The drift kinetic equation is challenging to solve numerically due to strong advection-dominance, recirculating flows, internal boundary layers, severe anisotropy, and high dimensionality. Fast and accurate solutions to the drift kinetic equation are required for high fidelity optimization, profile prediction, and analysis of experiments with uncertainty quantification. yancc solves both the full four-dimensional drift kinetic equation (retaining speed-dependent collisions, energy scattering, and full interspecies coupling), and the reduced monoenergetic form. The discretization combines a Maxwell polynomial collocation grid in speed with finite differences in pitch angle and the flux surface coordinates, using a modified upwind stencil designed to improve diagonal dominance for multigrid efficiency. The resulting linear system is solved with a multigrid-preconditioned Krylov method. Built in JAX, yancc is fully differentiable, enabling gradient-based optimization and adjoint sensitivity analysis. Benchmarks against MONKES and SFINCS show agreement within 1\% across a range of collisionalities, geometries, and multi-species configurations. yancc achieves roughly an order of magnitude speedup over SFINCS on a per-scan basis while using an order of magnitude less memory, with runtime remaining nearly flat across the full range of collisionality.

papers.title: Active methodologies for teaching historical processes and their relationship with critical thinking
papers.abstract: Research on active learning methodologies in history reveals discrepancies between the skills it claims to develop and the outcomes assessed, conflating performance, perceptions, and critical thinking. The objective was to analyze active learning methodologies used to teach historical processes and the evidence linking them to critical thinking. An exploratory scoping review of publications from 2020–2025 was conducted, using PRISMA-ScR as a reporting reference. A general web search engine identified 87 records; after removing duplicates and applying eligibility criteria, 18 publications were included. A descriptive and thematic synthesis was conducted. The approaches identified included document-based inquiry, problem-based learning, gamification, and digital activities. Improvements in specific aspects of historical performance and favorable perceptions were reported, although instruments and study designs varied. The evidence did not establish the superiority of any methodology or sustained transfer of critical thinking. The relationship examined depends on the tasks, measures, and designs employed. Direct assessments, comparators, and follow-up are needed. Search and selection limitations restrict the findings to an exploratory mapping of the literature.

papers.title: An Adaptive Machine Learning Framework for Early Lithium-Ion Battery Lifetime Prediction Under Heterogeneous Operating Conditions
papers.abstract: This study presents PAGER-Life, an adaptive hybrid framework for the early prediction of lithium-ion battery service life under heterogeneous operating conditions. The system integrates physically interpretable degradation features and standardized charge–discharge curves using linear regression, decision tree-based models, and neural networks. An error-aware routing mechanism combines expert predictions based on out-of-fold errors, while conformal prediction enables uncertainty quantification. The framework was evaluated using the MATR and HUST datasets with observation horizons of 20, 50, and 100 cycles, following a protocol that accounts for the grouped data structure and prevents information leakage. A comparative analysis involving 114 physical cells and 14 alternative methods demonstrated the following performance metrics for PAGER-Life: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 12.827%, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 166.766 cycles, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 210.715 cycles, and a macro-averaged coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.495. Ablation studies indicated that removing the physically grounded degradation features substantially degraded predictive performance. The results indicate that the adaptive integration of complementary prognostic models offers a promising approach for the early estimation of battery service life under heterogeneous operating conditions.

papers.abstract: This paper develops an adaptive model predictive control (AMPC) scheme for uncertain nonaffine nonlinear systems by integrating deep Koopman operator theory into a fully data-driven modeling framework. Complex nonlinear systems typically feature prominent nonaffine dynamics and are vulnerable to external disturbances, posing substantial difficulties for controller synthesis. Conventional Koopman-based methods depend on manually designed lifting functions, which suffer from limited modeling accuracy and heavy reliance on prior system knowledge. To address these deficiencies, this work adopts a deep neural network to autonomously learn optimal lifting dictionaries and construct a high-dimensional linear embedding of original nonlinear dynamics. This achieves global system linearization without parametric prior information and converts intractable nonaffine dynamics into a bilinear form amenable to linear control design. On this basis, model predictive control (MPC) is deployed as the core feedback module to guarantee closed-loop stability and satisfy system constraints via real-time receding horizon optimization. Furthermore, an iterative learning control (ILC) strategy is integrated to compensate for system uncertainties and external disturbances. The resulting composite control framework combines the real-time stabilizing merit of MPC and the iterative feedforward refinement capability of ILC across repeated operation trials. Rigorous convergence analysis based on the composite energy function theory verifies the asymptotic zero convergence of tracking errors for repetitive uncertainty components, while bounded residual error exists for non-repetitive disturbances. Comparative simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces modeling and tracking errors while preserving stable closed-loop performance. Quantitative evaluations further validate its superior precision and robustness over existing benchmark approaches, illustrating great applicability to complex nonlinear uncertain systems.

papers.abstract: Distributed antenna layouts optimized for nominal demand may deteriorate under changing hotspots and correlated shadowing. We present SA-MOBO-DAS, a scenario-aware multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework for placing four shared LTE/5G remote antenna units in a synthetic 500 × 500 m urban area. Its contribution is a placement and validation protocol combining worst-band coverage and throughput objectives, frozen operating scenarios, a fixed evaluation budget, and independent post-search risk assessment. A reproducible simulator incorporates 3GPP TR 38.901-inspired path loss, obstruction footprints, correlated shadowing, strongest power association, full-frequency reuse, and load-aware throughput at 2.1 GHz LTE and 3.5 GHz NR. Independent Matérn-5/2 Gaussian processes and a finite-pool approximation of q-noisy expected hypervolume improvement guide an 80-evaluation search. Thirty paired runs used 64 development and 160 held-out scenarios. SA-MOBO-DAS achieved held-out lower-tail hypervolume of 0.006619 (SD 0.000822), with no statistically detected difference from ParEGO (+0.7%; adjusted p = 0.968). Hypervolume exceeded NSGA-II and Sobol by 27.2% and 24.4%, respectively (both adjusted p < 0.001). Direct CVaR optimization yielded 7.6% and 0.9% higher point estimates of stress tail coverage and throughput, respectively, but reduced overall hypervolume by 10.6%. Paired 95% confidence intervals for both stress tail differences included zero.

papers.title: Design, implementation, and evaluation of an educational escape room for critical care learning among emergency medicine residents
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Traditional teaching methods often fail to adequately prepare emergency medicine (EM) residents for high-stakes critical care scenarios. Although gamified escape rooms show promise as active learning strategies, research has primarily focused on undergraduate learners. This study aimed to design, implement, and evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and perceived learning associated with a theory-informed educational escape room focused on critical care concepts. Methods This study was conducted at a medical Skills Laboratory (Tehran University of Medical Sciences) among EM residents with > 6 months of clinical experience. A theory-informed educational escape room was designed by a multidisciplinary team, integrating clinical scenarios, puzzles, and ACGME competencies. The intervention included the escape room simulation followed by a structured three-phase debriefing (reactions, scenario analysis, and summary). Data were collected to evaluate participants’ satisfaction with the educational escape room experience and their perceptions of learning. Results A structured, multistep process led to the development of an educational escape room for EM residents, comprising five scenario-based challenges aligned with core competencies in resuscitation, airway management, trauma management, anaphylaxis, and poisoning. Of 24 eligible residents, 9 (37.5%) volunteered to participate; 3 participated in the pilot session and 6 completed the final intervention. The intervention was successfully implemented in this small volunteer sample following pilot testing and subsequent refinements. In the final intervention group, high participant satisfaction was observed, with an overall mean ± SD score of 4.35 ± 0.41, including 4.42 ± 0.51 for the debriefing session, 4.23 ± 0.44 for the quality of the educational escape room and 4.5 ± 0.45 for alignment with learners’ needs. Perceived learning was also rated favorably, with a mean ± SD score of 4.30 ± 0.53 in the final intervention group. Conclusion This pilot evaluation suggests that a structured, scenario-based educational escape room can be implemented in a small volunteer sample of EM residents and was well received by participants. Participants reported high satisfaction with the escape room experience and favorable perceptions of learning.

papers.title: Adaptive Variable-Set Model Predictive Control with Error-Dynamics and Current-Stress Awareness for Dual-Active-Bridge Converters
papers.abstract: Dual-Active-Bridge (DAB) DC-DC converters are widely used in modern power electronics applications due to their bidirectional power flow, high efficiency, and electrical isolation. However, traditional linear controllers are highly sensitive to parameter variations, which can degrade control performance under changing operating conditions. In addition, conventional Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control (FCS-MPC) methods may result in relatively high current and voltage ripple under steady-state conditions. Furthermore, existing Moving Discrete Control Set (MDCS-MPC) strategies can only partially address these issues because they have a fixed or limited control set. To address these problems, this paper proposes an Error-Dynamics and Current-Stress-Aware Adaptive Variable-Size Moving Control Set MPC (ED-AVCS-MPC) for DAB converters. In this article, using the example of a single-phase shift-operated dual-active-bridge converter, the proposed control design is explained in detail and analyzed thoroughly. The proposed strategy employs a composite activation index that continuously evaluates both the magnitude and the rate of change in the voltage error. Thus, the control set size (3, 5, or 7 elements) is dynamically adjusted via a hysteresis-based switching mechanism. A five-term dynamically weighted cost function is formulated to simultaneously penalize tracking deviation, voltage variation, excessive control effort, current stress, and boundary violations. Through comprehensive simulation studies, the superiority of the ED-AVCS-MPC over traditional PI and fixed-set MDCS-MPC approaches has been confirmed.

Competency assessment using a structured rubric ( κ = 0.78 inter-rater reliability) indicated that students demonstrated systems thinking, simulation modeling, industrial automation, and evidence-based decision-making. Cohort-level simulation outputs ranged from 720 to 850 units (mean = 789, SD = 38), with 14/18 teams identifying common capacity-mismatch challenges. The framework offers a potentially adaptable model for integrating Industry 4.0 technologies into engineering curricula, preparing students for the technological and human-centered challenges of contemporary manufacturing.

papers.title: Toward a Theory of Granular Digital Twins: Mathematical Foundations for Adaptive Digital Twin Systems
papers.abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology models and synchronizes physical systems through virtual counterparts. Existing mathematical formulations of DTs concentrate on physical-virtual synchronization and say little about how representations of the same system at different levels of detail should be related. This paper builds a mathematical foundation for Granular Digital Twins (GDTs) by combining Granular Computing with DT theory. We introduce information granules, the Granular Representation Mapping, the Granular Twin Space, and the Granular Digital Twin, and then construct a Granular Twin Algebra whose aggregation, refinement, and adaptive transformation operators act on an ordered family of granular representations. The structure is analyzed through lattice properties, Granular Twin Homomorphisms, adaptive granular evolution, and granular equilibrium. When the representation family is a complete lattice and the adaptive transformation is order-preserving, the Knaster-Tarski theorem guarantees that the set of granular equilibria is non-empty and is itself a complete lattice; each equilibrium is invariant under repeated adaptive transformation. These results are existence and invariance results only; uniqueness, convergence, and dynamical stability are not claimed. The framework moves DT theory from state-oriented synchronization toward adaptive granular representation and gives a formal basis for organizing hierarchical information in DT systems.

papers.title: Pressure-dependent spectral-moment-constrained physics-informed neural-network WSGG model for multi-species gas mixtures
papers.abstract: Radiative heat transfer in combustion over varying pressures is strongly affected by the nongray absorption of participating gases, making efficient and accurate radiation modeling essential for combustion simulations involving radiative heat transfer. This work develops a pressure-dependent, spectral-moment-constrained physics-informed neural-network weighted-sum-of-gray-gases (PINN-WSGG) model for H 2 O–CO 2 –CO mixtures. Total pressure is introduced as an explicit input, and Planck-weighted spectral moments are incorporated to constrain the gray-gas decomposition. The model covers temperatures from 300 to 3000 K, pressures from 0.1 to 80 bar, and arbitrary mole-fraction combinations of H 2 O, CO 2 , and CO. Validation against line-by-line-based one-dimensional benchmarks, conventional pressure-dependent WSGG models, and full-spectrum correlated- 𝑘 (FSCK) calculations shows that the model maintains high accuracy over this wide parameter range and improves radiative heat-loss predictions. Applications to a laboratory flame and an industrial gas turbine combustor further demonstrate reliable radiative heat transfer predictions with negligible spectral-parameter evaluation overhead. The proposed model provides a compact and practical approach for nongray radiation modeling under diverse combustion conditions.

papers.title: Geospatial AI for flood susceptibility mapping: a systematic literature review of parameters, methods, uncertainty quantification, and resilience frameworks
papers.abstract: Over the last decade and a half, flood susceptibility mapping (FSM) has evolved from bivariate statistics to ensemble machine learning and deep learning, but it still does not fully meet the requirements of calibrated, probabilistic outputs required by stochastic flood risk assessment. This systematic literature review (SLR) compiles 200 peer-reviewed FSM studies (2010–2024) from 4,624 records across six databases and performs a quality-appraisal for them using a purpose-built instrument (FSM-QAC) comprising 14 criteria, to answer 5 research questions related to methodological evolution, conditioning parameter hierarchies, validation integrity, uncertainty quantification, and integration of climate-resilience. A three-phase methodological evolution is documented, ranging from statistical frameworks (mean area under the curve [AUC]: 0.81–0.83) to ensemble machine learning (0.89–0.92) to deep learning and hybrid architectures (0.93–0.96), and a ceiling of discriminative accuracy is observed. Based on the evidence, there is a four-level conditioning parameter hierarchy, with elevation, slope, Topographic Wetness Index (TWI), and distance-from-river being universally indispensable Tier 1 parameters. Four major limitations are found: 73% of studies report AUC values that are inflated by an estimated 0.05 units due to the use of spatially naive validation designs; 48% of studies report no uncertainty-quantified outputs; only 6% report probabilistic calibration metrics; and 63.5% of studies do not integrate future climate projections. The evidence base has developed in a methodologically sound way, but has not yet moved from AUC-optimised deterministic mapping to a calibrated, spatially validated and climate-adaptive probabilistic flood risk science that is required for decision making. Twenty research gaps that are grounded in the empirical evidence are identified, and twelve directions are identified as priorities to guide that transition.

We assessed this reporting evidence using a five-dimension framework (accuracy reporting, uncertainty quantification, spatial validation, temporal consistency and transparency) applied to a systematically identified set of empirical studies. From 1706 records retrieved from Scopus and Lens.org on 4 March 2026, 1146 unique works were screened against a locked eligibility codebook; 153 reports were assessed in full text where accessible, and 59 empirical ML/DL remote-sensing AGB studies in tropical or subtropical forests formed the core review set. For each dimension we coded evidence as confirmed, reported as absent, insufficient or inaccessible, and report the share of studies between the confirmed count and the confirmed-plus-undetermined count. Accuracy metrics were reported in 66–88% of studies, but spatially independent validation was confirmed in only 32–42%, spatially explicit or area-level uncertainty in 44–54%, multi-date analysis with an explicit consistency method in 14–22%, public code in 14–29% and public reference data in 15–29%. papers.title: Need for Speed: Fast and Accurate Pricing of American Options Using Parameterized Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: The financial world and the field of quantitative finance face the challenge of accurate and rapid valuation of American-style options, particularly in high-frequency trading and market-making environments. In this study, we propose a deep-learning-based framework for pricing American options using Parameterized Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PPINNs). The proposed approach extends standard PINNs by incorporating key model parameters (strike price, volatility, and interest rate) as network inputs, along with the standard practice of using stock price and time to maturity as PINN inputs. The modified structure is called Parameterized-PINNs. It retains the physics-informed formulation of PINNs by incorporating the governing partial differential equation into the learning process while enabling a single trained network to generalize across a broad range of option configurations without requiring retraining. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high average pricing accuracy, with an L2 relative error of approximately 0.20% for call options and 0.09% for put options, over the full evaluation domain. However, local relative errors in deep out-of-the-money regions under extreme parameter combinations can be substantially higher, primarily due to near-zero option values rather than large absolute mispricings. Once trained with a one-time offline cost of approximately 65 min for call options or 71 min for put options, PPINN inference takes almost 1.5 ms per option, approximately 1000 times faster than the Monte Carlo benchmark in the reported single-option evaluation, making it well suited to applications requiring repeated revaluation across a stable parameter regime. The framework is further evaluated using 1500 observed American option prices for two actively traded U.S. equities (Tesla and Amazon). The market-data experiment provides an additional empirical assessment of practical applicability. Overall, the numerical experiments demonstrate that PPINNs can provide accurate and low-latency approximations to the specified Black–Scholes American option pricing problem, with potential applicability to repeated valuation under stable model assumptions.

papers.title: When Human Tissue Meets the Driveline: Implications of Tissue Integration to Combat Driveline Infections
papers.abstract: Driveline infection remains a common complication of ventricular assist device (VAD) therapy. These infections often progress from the exit site through the subcutaneous tract to the deeper tunnel and, in severe cases, the pocket, underscoring the vulnerability of the driveline–tissue interface. In this review, we examine the biological and mechanical factors governing tissue-driveline interactions and their implications for tissue integration of the implanted driveline. Dysregulated inflammation, impaired vascular maturation, abnormal extracellular matrix remodeling, repetitive micromotion and traction, and biomaterial–tissue mismatch may all compromise optimal tissue ingrowth of the driveline. Insufficient tissue integration can lead to the formation of microgaps within the driveline tunnel, providing a potential niche for microbial colonization and biofilm formation, thereby contributing to persistent driveline infections. Recognizing the potential association between inadequate tissue integration and the occurrence of driveline infection shifts the focus from microbial eradication alone toward optimizing driveline–tissue interactions across different segments of the driveline. Such an approach may help reduce the incidence of driveline infections in patients requiring long-term VAD support. Finally, strategies to promote tissue integration and long-term driveline stability, including driveline surface engineering, modulation of physicochemical properties, and optimization of surgical techniques, are discussed.

To solve this, we applied an efficient Gaussian Process Bayesian Optimization (GP-BO) framework to optimize submerged fermentation using Lactobacillus brevis (VTCC 12248). Key factors—inoculum size, initial pH, and fermentation time—were systematically refined across just 15 targeted runs in three sequential rounds. The model identified peak fermentation parameters at a 5.25% v/v inoculum, an initial pH of 5.35, and an incubation time of 38.0 hours. Experimental validation under these conditions produced 6.48±0.18 mg/g of GABA per gram of dry substrate, matching model predictions with a low 0.61% relative error while achieving high probiotic cell counts (9.47\log_{10}{\text{CFU/mL}}) and an 88.42% precursor conversion rate. Sensory evaluation by 30 consumer panelists confirmed that controlled fermentation preserved ST25's natural aroma while significantly enhancing overall taste acceptability from 6.85 to 7.60 on a 9-point Hedonic scale p < 0.001). Compared to conventional Response Surface Methodology, the GP-BO approach reduced experimental time and material costs by over 60%, offering a streamlined blueprint for transforming regional cereal crops into functional food ingredients.

papers.title: WarfaRisk: A Reproducible, Fairness-Aware Machine Learning Pipeline for Warfarin Dose Prediction (Prototype)
papers.abstract: Warfarin dosing is complicated by wide inter-patient variability driven by genetic, demographic, and pharmacological factors. Although machine learning approaches to dose prediction have been widely studied, published evaluations are frequently affected by analysis-domain data leakage, small held-out sets, and an absence of calibration and fairness assessment across ancestry subgroups. We describe WarfaRisk, a nine-phase open-source machine learning pipeline for warfarin dose prediction evaluated on two public International Warfarin Pharmacogenetics Consortium (IWPC) cohorts (n=6037 and n=1780, the latter a non-independent secondary consistency check) using fixed patient-level splits and a single documented random seed. The pipeline incorporates leakage-free preprocessing, nested clinical and pharmacogenomic feature ablation across nine model architectures, leave-one-ancestry-out portability assessment with a cross-model robustness check, conformal prediction calibration reported at subgroup resolution, and individual-level SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) feature attribution. The nine-architecture ablation results reported here are from the primary cohort, IWPC-6256; the complete two-cohort comparison is reported in a companion evaluation manuscript. A prototype web-based clinical decision support interface integrates dose recommendation, uncertainty quantification, and SHAP explainability with a Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) R4 endpoint. In preliminary evaluation on a single fixed held-out split, Model Agnostic Prediction Interval Estimator (MAPIE) cross-conformal (5-fold CV+) prediction achieves coverage close to its nominal target when measured across each cohort as a whole. When this coverage is instead stratified by ancestry, a different pattern emerges: coverage for African-ancestry patients falls well short, a gap the aggregate number hides, plausibly explained by alleles missing from the standard IWPC genotype panel and supported by independent pharmacogenetic literature, though not directly demonstrated in this dataset. These findings indicate that subgroup-level calibration reporting is necessary, not optional, since its absence can let a model appear well-calibrated in aggregate while failing a specific population in practice.

papers.title: Teachers’ Educational Psychology Knowledge and English Language Teaching Practices in Malawian Primary Schools
papers.abstract: Educational psychology equips teachers with knowledge of learner cognition, motivation, emotional development, and behavior management, thereby supporting effective instructional delivery and learner-centered pedagogy. Despite national reforms promoting active learning in Malawi, many primary classrooms remain constrained by overcrowding, inadequate teaching and learning materials, and persistent teacher-centered practices that limit learner engagement and classroom effectiveness. This study investigated how teachers’ educational psychology knowledge shapes English language pedagogy, learner engagement, and classroom effectiveness in Malawi’s primary education context. A descriptive cross-sectional design with a convergent mixed-methods approach was employed, combining structured questionnaires and systematic classroom observations. All twenty (20) English language teachers teaching Standards 1 to 4 at Dzenza Primary School, Lilongwe District, participated via census sampling. Quantitative data were analyzed using frequencies and percentages; qualitative data were analyzed thematically. Teachers reported strong awareness of educational psychology principles and their positive influence on the use of Teaching and Learning Materials (TLMs) (100%), varied instructional methods (100%), understanding of individual learner differences (100%), reinforcement techniques (100%), and guidance and counseling (100%). Implementation was significantly constrained by inadequate TLMs (80%), limited lesson time (75%), overcrowded classrooms, and learner misbehavior (85%). Classroom observations confirmed use of learner-centered strategies when resources permitted, alongside persistent teacher-centered approaches in overcrowded conditions. Teachers possess considerable educational psychology knowledge, but a structural mediation effect was identified: systemic barriers including overcrowding, resource scarcity, and insufficient professional development systematically constrain the translation of psychological competence into sustained learner-centered practice. The study advances the argument that educational psychology knowledge functions as a necessary but insufficient condition for effective ELT in low-resource African contexts. Continuous professional development, TLM provision, reduced class sizes, and stronger integration of multilingual and structural dimensions into teacher training are recommended.

papers.title: Research on path tracking control of human-machine co-driving vehicles based on game theory

Through joint simulation verification, the extended Kalman filter with better estimation performance is selected. Then, an adaptive model predictive controller and a single-point preview driver model are constructed for path tracking at different speeds. The controller time-domain parameters are selected using the approach to ideal value sorting method, and the adaptive MPC and driver model are compared with nonlinear model predictive control and a linear quadratic regulator, respectively. Finally, for the dynamic allocation of human-machine lateral driving authority, a driving authority allocation model based on game theory is constructed. The human-machine participation index, comfort index, vehicle anti-collision index, and human-machine conflict confrontation index are comprehensively considered to optimize the control weight allocation from multiple dimensions. The Nash product is used to solve the equilibrium strategy. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the game-based authority allocation strategy, while real-vehicle tests demonstrate the feasibility of the path-tracking control framework.

This creates a complex and pressing challenge in cardio-oncology: how to treat cancer, while minimising harm to the heart effectively. A central goal in cardio-oncology is therefore not only to understand the mechanisms of therapy-induced cardiac injury, but also to develop reliable, and predictive approaches to detect and assess CTR-CVT as early as possible, ideally before irreversible damage occurs. Advantages and limitations are addressed for each experimental model to help guide future studies in cardiooncology that might better translate findings from the bench to the bedside.

papers.title: Monte Carlo–Informed Surrogate Model for the Analysis of Decay Heat Behavior in Molten Salt Reactors
papers.abstract: Noble metal fission products in molten salt reactors (MSRs) deposit on primary loop surfaces, where their decay heat becomes safety-relevant during drain scenarios: Once the salt is discharged, the deposit remains without active cooling and can drive localized overheating. Predicting it requires tracking the full nuclide inventory across core, bulk, and deposition regions, for which repeated Monte Carlo (MC) depletion is prohibitive. This work develops a MC-informed surrogate built on a sparse transition operator spanning neutron-induced reactions, decay, advection, and deposition, with region-wise mass transfer correlations setting the deposition rates. The neutron-induced rates are extracted from a single MC simulation and rescaled with power under a constant-spectrum assumption, so that the ordinary differential equations (ODEs) system is solved without further transport runs, for a substantially larger nuclide set than historical zero-dimensional models. Applied to the Molten Salt Reactor Experiment (MSRE) fuel loop, the predicted mass transfer coefficients reproduce the original MSRE values, and the calculated 132Te distribution is comparable across surfaces for both the 233U and 235U campaigns without per-nuclide tuning. Benchmarked against a self-consistent MC workflow on a simplified generic MSR case, the surrogate reproduces the total decay heat of both the bulk and deposition nodes from sub-second to yearly time scales, to within ±0.3% at fixed power and ~2% under sinusoidal modulation. It does so at a cost low enough for design exploration and for a digital-twin representation of the primary loop. An uncertainty quantification shows that fission yields dominate the nuclear data budget and that the deposited inventory is markedly more uncertain than the bulk, partly due to non–noble-metal precursors in the yield normalization constraint.

The results indicate that increasing scan speed leads to higher martensite content but adversely affects tensile strength and hardness. In contrast, the annealing stage refined the microstructure, enhancing ductility and promoting phase homogenization. While quenching followed by tempering improved toughness and wear resistance, it was accompanied by a reduction in tensile strength. Notably, a 1200% increase in impact toughness was observed after tempering at the lowest scan speed, despite a slight decrease in wear resistance. papers.title: Swarm-optimized heterogeneous ensemble with quantile regression for small-sample long-tailed distribution prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting maintenance costs for industrial equipment faces the dual challenges of small sample sizes and long-tailed data distributions. Existing methods struggle to ensure both point prediction accuracy and reliable intervals for the tail. This paper proposes the Swarm-driven Adaptive Data Augmentation and Heterogeneous Ensemble with Distribution-Aware Quantile Fusion (SADA-HEDQF) framework. In the SADA stage, Differential Evolution automatically derives high-order features within a domain-specific operator space, and Particle Swarm Optimization optimizes the parameters of the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique, enhancing data from both feature and sample dimensions. In the HEDQF stage, a multi-objective Whale Optimization Algorithm constructs a decorrelated heterogeneous base learner pool, and a Quantile Long Short-Term Memory network is designed as the gated fusion meta-learner. Driven by the quantile loss, the meta-learner simultaneously outputs point estimates and multiple confidence intervals. Experiments on 673 real ship maintenance records demonstrate that SADA-HEDQF reduces the point prediction RMSE by 25.8% compared to the best single model, and the error in high-cost regions drops by 46.4%. The normalized average width of the 90% confidence interval is 0.379, and the Coverage Width-based Criterion with penalty on the tail subset reaches 294.5, both significantly outperforming benchmarks such as Quantile Regression Forest. Ablation studies and SHAP analysis quantify the layered contributions of each component and verify the physical interpretability of the derived features, respectively. The framework provides effective prediction and uncertainty quantification support for small-sample long-tailed regression tasks, such as ship maintenance cost prediction, and shows potential for transfer to similar structured prediction scenarios.

papers.title: A Hybrid physics-informed digital twin for offshore wind-farm flow prediction: integrating CFD simulations with deep regression forest and probabilistic surrogate models
papers.abstract: Abstract The marine-atmosphere dynamics are nonlinear and multiscale, which poses a computational challenge for accurately describing the flow field around offshore wind turbines. Using advanced data-driven surrogate models and CFD simulations, this study presents a hybrid physics-informed digital twin framework to predict wind farm behavior under stochastic environmental conditions with high accuracy. In this work, we propose a framework that simultaneously integrates spatiotemporal dependencies, physical constraints, and probabilistic uncertainties by combining Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), Deep-Gaussian Process Regression (Deep-GPR), Extreme Gradient Boosting Algorithm (XGBoost), and a transformer-based regression model called CFD-Former. PINNs incorporate Navier–Stokes equation residuals into the training process to ensure physical consistency, while XGBoost and Deep-GPR improve model generalizability to different inlet flow conditions. Hybrid surrogate models are trained on data from CFD calculations with different wind direction and speed conditions. The generated digital twin is able to predict the velocities measured at the meteorological tower within an uncertainty of 10% and reproduce the high resolution flow patterns due to CFD with a mean absolute deviation below 1%. This novel approach uses deterministic simulation and intelligent inference to predict offshore wind farm performance in a scalable and physically based manner, possibly enabling adaptive operation and reliability assessment.

Two integration strategies are considered to introduce an innovative class of interpenetrating architectures: full integration across the heat exchanger domain, and partial integration selectively confined to a single fluid domain. Three-dimensional conjugate heat transfer analyses are conducted for 48 configurations with different volume-fraction combinations. The baseline-geometry results were compared with experimentally-validated reference data to assess the accuracy of the numerical model. The results for the hybrid configurations are compared against their pure TPMS counterparts to evaluate the effects of lattice hybridization on heat transfer, pressure loss, and overall thermo–hydraulic performance. The results indicate that, for the investigated designs, partial integration reduces the frictional penalty in the unobstructed fluid domain compared with full integration. In the partial-integration configurations, the secondary lattice is placed in the S-CO 2 domain for the Schwarz-Primitive base and in the cooling-water domain for the Gyroid base, leaving the opposing fluid domain unobstructed. Among the investigated designs, the partially integrated Schwarz-Primitive-Diamond configuration achieved the highest overall thermo–hydraulic performance, with a performance evaluation criterion of 4.52, corresponding to a 3.5-times improvement relative to a smooth-tube reference. This paper proposes a model predictive control (MPC)-based coordinated frequency support strategy for renewable power plants integrating wind power, photovoltaic (PV) generation, and hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs). An equivalent grid frequency response model is first established and combined with aggregated dynamic models of wind, PV, and heterogeneous HESS units to develop a unified control-oriented state-space formulation. In this framework, renewable reserve limits, storage power constraints, and state-of-charge (SoC) dynamics are explicitly incorporated to characterize the time-varying feasible support capability of the plant. On this basis, the coordinated frequency support problem is formulated as a constrained receding-horizon optimization problem, in which frequency deviation suppression, plant-level supplementary power coordination, and HESS energy-state management are considered simultaneously. Simulation studies under step-change and random load disturbances demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy. Under the representative step-change disturbance, the maximum frequency deviation is limited to approximately 4.5×10−4 p.u., and the frequency rapidly recovers to a steady operating region. Under random load disturbances, the frequency deviation remains bounded within approximately ±1.0×10−3 p.u. Moreover, the SoC values of all heterogeneous storage units remain within the prescribed range of 0.3–0.7 p.u. throughout the support process. These results demonstrate that the proposed strategy achieves effective transient frequency support while maintaining coordinated active power allocation and feasible HESS energy-state operation.

papers.title: Interface-Controlled Wellbore Leakage in CCUS Wells: Microannulus Formation, Pathway Evolution, Detection, and Risks
papers.abstract: Wellbore integrity is central to geological CO2 storage because wells can intersect formations intended to contain injected CO2 and displaced brine. This critical narrative review examines how defects at casing–cement and cement–formation interfaces form, evolve, and contribute to hydraulic communication and potential leakage. Laboratory experiments, field observations, numerical models, and diagnostic studies are compared with attention to what each type of evidence can establish. Cement alteration, structural debonding, measurable fluid movement, and consequential leakage are distinct observations. Interface conductance depends on hydraulic aperture, connectivity, effective stress, thermal and pressure cycling, fluid chemistry, and flow history; mechanical closure or precipitation may restrict pathways, whereas renewed loading or dissolution may preserve or enlarge them. Diagnostic interpretations require method- and well-specific calibration: an undetected anomaly does not establish zero flow. Brine migration, dissolved-CO2 transport, and free-phase CO2 entry have different pressure, capillary, and saturation controls. The proposed interface-to-risk framework links defect evidence, exposure, phase-specific migration, and possible receptor consequences without treating the framework as a calibrated risk model. Priorities include cyclic testing, coupled multiphase characterization, field validation, and laboratory-to-field uncertainty quantification.

papers.abstract: Abstract Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) is highly vulnerable to a range of process-induced defects that can adversely part quality, structural integrity, dimensional accuracy and long-term reliability, thereby limiting broader industrial adoption. This work presents a feasibility investigation into automated detection of defect-related surface patterns in LPBF using a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based image classification framework. Classical image-processing techniques were initially found to be insufficient for reliable defect detection due to their limited robustness to variations in surface morphologies and image characteristics. To address these limitations, a CNN-based image classification framework was developed and trained using surrogate-labeled LPBF surface images to evaluate the viability of deep learning for automated surface condition classification and recognition. The proposed and developed model achieved a validation accuracy of approximately 84% while exhibiting stable convergence behavior during training, indicating that meaningful classification of LPBF surface patterns is achievable under limited labeling conditions, demonstrating the potential of deep learning for automated LPBF surface condition assessment. This work establishes a foundation for future work focused on incorporating physically verified defect labels, improved imaging fidelity, and integration with in-situ monitoring framework to enable real-time defect detection in LPBF process conforming for quality assurance.

papers.abstract: This review explores the integration of value engineering (VE) and Bayesian inference models as a strategic optimization framework for enhancing benefits realization across portfolio-level project management. With increasing demands for delivering measurable value in complex project portfolios, organizations are turning to probabilistic and data-driven methods to align project outcomes with strategic objectives. Value engineering offers a systematic approach to optimizing functions and cost-efficiency, while Bayesian inference provides robust capabilities in uncertainty quantification, real-time learning, and predictive modeling. This paper synthesizes existing literature on VE applications in portfolio management and examines the role of Bayesian networks and decision theory in forecasting project benefit probabilities, stakeholder satisfaction, and lifecycle outcomes. Furthermore, it discusses the integration of these methodologies into benefits realization frameworks and governance models. Case studies and modeling insights are analyzed to highlight best practices, methodological advancements, and implementation barriers. The review concludes by proposing a scalable architecture for dynamic portfolio optimization using VE and Bayesian inference.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Solubility Enhancement of Poorly Water-Soluble Drugs: From Solubility Prediction to Formulation Optimization
papers.abstract: Poor aqueous solubility limits the development of many orally administered drug candidates, particularly those in Biopharmaceutics Classification System (BCS) class II and, in some cases, class IV. Conventional solubility-enhancement approaches, including particle-size reduction, solid dispersions, amorphous systems, lipid-based formulations, cyclodextrin complexation, nanocrystals, salt formation and pharmaceutical cocrystals, are effective but often require extensive, formulation-specific experimentation. Growing pharmaceutical datasets and advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) now offer predictive, data-driven support. Models have been reported for predicting aqueous and formulation-phase solubility, screening drug-excipient combinations, estimating drug-polymer interaction, optimizing compositions and predicting dissolution or supersaturation behaviour. Bayesian optimization, active learning and surrogate modelling are being explored to reduce the number of formulation experiments, and integration with physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modelling, Quality by Design (QbD) and automated experimentation may further support rational development. However, small and heterogeneous datasets, experimental variability, limited interpretability and external validation, data leakage and uncertain regulatory acceptance remain significant barriers. This review discusses AI and ML in the solubility enhancement of poorly water-soluble drugs, progressing from molecular solubility prediction to drug-excipient selection, advanced formulation design and formulation optimization. Particular emphasis is placed on experimentally validated applications and on the distinction between computational prediction and demonstrated pharmaceutical performance. Current challenges, research gaps and opportunities for reliable, explainable and experimentally integrated AI-driven formulation platforms are outlined.

papers.title: Confidence-aware learning for real-time optimal terminal guidance with impact time constraints
papers.abstract: Constrained real-time optimal terminal guidance is essential for high-precision strike missions of missiles, but is limited by onboard computational constraints. Data-driven supervised learning has therefore emerged as an alternative to numerical optimization by enabling fast online inference through offline training. However, its deployment for guidance problems is still limited by two challenges. First, learning-based guidance relies on large-scale optimal datasets, while existing numerical optimal control solvers often lack sufficient efficiency and stability to generate scalable and well-distributed training data. Second, most learning-based guidance networks operate as black-box models whose outputs strongly depend on training data distribution, making it difficult to guarantee reliability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a confidence-aware learning framework for optimal terminal guidance with impact time constraints. An improved backward integration data generation method guided by the state transition matrix is developed to achieve efficient and uniform coverage of the desired state space. An error distribution smoothing method is further introduced to construct a lightweight dataset for Gaussian process regression with uncertainty quantification. Finally, a confidence-weighted combined guidance strategy is designed by adaptively fusing the learned policy with an analytical guidance law. Numerical simulations demonstrate the optimality and reliability of the proposed approach for constrained terminal guidance.

papers.title: Dynamic Programming-Compatible Uncertainty Sets in Robust Markov Decision Processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the compatibility of robust Markov decision processes (RMDPs) with dynamic programming under various assumptions on the uncertainty set (i.e., we investigate when one can solve an RMDP by solving a fixed-point equation. We show that in all generality, s-rectangular and sa-rectangular uncertainty sets are the only models of uncertainty that are compatible with dynamic programming. Our analysis shows that existing nonrectangular models, including r-rectangularity, are only weakly compatible with dynamic programming as they require the assumption that rewards do not depend on the next state. In this case, our results imply that one can always construct a rectangular uncertainty set that is equivalent for both policy evaluation and optimization to the dynamic programming-compatible nonrectangular model. This highlights a key limitation; dynamic-programming-compatible nonrectangular uncertainty sets, although practically relevant for uncertainty quantification, do not provide a genuinely distinct assessment of policy performance. Interestingly, our proof techniques rely on identifying a novel simultaneous solvability property, which we show is central to several important properties of RMDPs, including the existence of stationary optimal policies and dynamic programming-based formulations. The simultaneous solvability property enables a unified approach to studying all existing models of uncertainty, rectangular and nonrectangular alike. papers.title: Module-level grid-side power-quality comparison of SiC-based three-phase AC-DC converter topologies for modular high-power EV charging
papers.abstract: This paper compares three SiC–based three-phase AC–DC power converter topologies for modular high-power electric vehicle (EV) charging applications: (i) Bidirectional two-level full-bridge; (ii) Unidirectional three-level Vienna rectifier; and (iii) Bidirectional three-level t-type converter. The study targets module-level operation in high-power modular EV chargers and mainly focuses on analyzing the grid-side power quality, quantified by total harmonic distortion (THD) and ripple of the current. This comparison makes use of a deadbeat predictive current controller, implemented as a continuous-control-set model predictive control (CCS-MPC) scheme, common to the three topologies. Simulations are carried out with up to six 100 kW AC-DC modules in parallel, both without phase shift and with a carrier phase shift of 360°/ n between AC-DC modules. The results show that the inclusion of phase shift significantly reduces the grid-side current THD in the full-bridge and t-type power converters, which makes it practically independent of the number of AC-DC modules, whereas the Vienna rectifier maintains significantly higher THD values due to the uncontrollable region associated with the diodes. Finally, experimental results are obtained using a 25 kW reduced scale prototype common to the three studied topologies, considering the operation of a single AC-DC converter module and evaluating grid-side power quality under identical operating conditions.

papers.abstract: Abstract Wheat middlings are a heterogeneous byproduct from wheat milling, representing 30.0 wt % of the wheat kernel. It can contain 20.0 wt % starch and 13.7 wt % crude protein (dry basis), along with cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin, and inorganics. In this work, we present washing processes designed to maximize the removal of starch and crude protein from wheat middlings. papers.title: Data-driven forecasting of cross-border power flows across NEMO cable using machine learning and statistical techniques
papers.abstract: This study investigates short-term electricity flow forecasting for the NEMO Link interconnector between Belgium and Great Britain. The goal is to support effective grid operation and energy trading. Using a step-by-step approach, the study generated 48-hour-ahead forecasts and evaluated three modelling techniques, namely Autoregressive Moving Average with eXogenous inputs (ARMAX), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM). The performance of these models was evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and the Coefficient of Determination ( R 2 ). The models were evaluated after feature engineering and careful model selection. The results show that all three models provide accurate predictions over the test period, with R 2 values of at least 0.94. ARMAX achieved the lowest numerical RMSE and MAE over the three-month test period and the lowest numerical errors for the representative 48-hour recursive forecasting window. Statistical comparison using the Diebold–Mariano (DM) and Harvey–Leybourne–Newbold (HLN)-corrected DM tests provided a balanced assessment of model performance across different evaluation periods. In addition, rolling-origin validation demonstrated that forecasting performance varies with the forecasting period while remaining robust across multiple evaluation windows. Bootstrap-based 95% prediction intervals were constructed to quantify forecasting uncertainty. These results highlight the value of combining feature selection, recursive forecasting, rolling-origin validation, uncertainty quantification, and statistical significance testing for reliable short-term interconnector flow forecasting.

papers.title: Intelligent Building Energy Control Systems: A Review of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Technologies, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Improving energy efficiency and reducing environmental impact are among the most significant global challenges today. In particular, building energy systems (BESs) are the main consumers of urban energy. Reducing energy consumption and optimizing the operation of BESs can help conserve energy resources. Traditional rule-based controllers (RBCs) are limited in their ability to optimize building energy consumption while maintaining occupant comfort. Data-driven model predictive control (MPC), which uses building thermal dynamic models and historical data for training, may struggle to handle uncertain cases. Reinforcement learning (RL) allows the control systems to make decisions in real time. However, when the system becomes scalable, training a single agent becomes complicated and more time-consuming. Therefore, multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) methods are being investigated and applied to building-related energy systems. This paper provides a comprehensive literature review of recent advancements in MARL control methods for building-related energy systems and evaluates their adaptability, complexity, and realization. This review paper identifies current challenges and future directions in this field.

papers.title: Hierarchical MPC–QP Control for Primary Frequency Regulation of a Wind–Storage Hybrid System with Intra-Farm Power Optimization
papers.abstract: High penetration of wind power increases the need for coordinated frequency support from wind farms and battery energy storage systems (BESSs). To address insufficient power coordination, state-of-charge (SOC) deviation, and suboptimal intra-farm allocation of frequency-regulation power, this paper proposes a hierarchical MPC–QP control strategy for primary frequency regulation of a wind–storage hybrid system. At the upper level, model predictive control (MPC) minimizes system frequency deviation and a composite frequency-regulation cost index subject to wind-farm power, BESS power, and SOC constraints, thereby determining optimal regulation-power references for the wind farm and BESS. At the lower level, quadratic programming (QP) minimizes wind-farm regulation-power tracking error and equivalent torque fluctuations to achieve differentiated power allocation among equivalent turbine clusters. In a representative 1 h simulation with continuously varying wind speed and random load disturbances, the proposed strategy reduces the RMS frequency deviation, maximum absolute frequency deviation, RMS SOC deviation, and cumulative regulation cost index by 24.20%, 24.53%, 93.86%, and 84.72%, respectively, compared with PI control. Compared with equal allocation, it reduces the RMS wind-farm power-tracking error and RMS equivalent torque fluctuation by 87.93% and 15.52%, respectively. Three additional stochastic realizations demonstrate consistent improvements in the selected performance indices, further supporting the effectiveness of the proposed hierarchical strategy under the investigated simulation conditions.
